articleTitle: Neural Networks for Financial Fraud Detection: Enhancing Security with Scalable Machine Learning and Deep learning Solutions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: As financial fraud evolves, conventional methods struggle to counter increasingly sophisticated schemes. This paper presents an AI-powered system focused on fraud detection, utilizing neural networks for enhanced adaptability and computational efficiency. The proposed system processes extensive financial datasets in real-time, employing a variety of machine learning models such as Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Machines, Support Vector Machines, and deep learning approaches like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks. These techniques excel in identifying intricate fraud patterns by analysing both structured and unstructured data sources, including transaction records, financial databases, and customer information. Neural networks enable the system to dynamically adjust and optimize its detection capabilities while minimizing reliance on traditional data storage systems by efficiently compressing large volumes of financial data. The adaptability of the system ensures it can quickly respond to new fraud trends and regulatory requirements, making it a forward-looking solution for combating fraud.This paper outlines the architecture, implementation, and methodology behind the proposed neural network-driven AI system. A detailed evaluation shows significant improvements in accuracy, processing speed, and system scalability when compared to traditional fraud detection methods. Neural networks, through ensemble learning, enhance the system’s ability to integrate various models, resulting in a more effective approach to detecting fraud in real time. This new framework offers a robust alternative to conventional methods, combining machine learning, deep learning, and neural networks for an advanced, scalable, and secure fraud detection system.

articleTitle: Time based Sentiment Analysis of Financial Headlines using Recurrent Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The sentiment of financial news headlines plays an important role in understanding market trends and investor behavior. This study proposes a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN)-based model for accurately classifying the sentiment of financial headlines into positive, neutral, and negative categories. Keeping in mind the time trend based behavior of the financial world, and the impact of certain keywords relevant only in the financial context, the RNN architecture captures the contextual nuances often overlooked by traditional methods. To address the domain-specific challenges of financial language and the inherent trends based on the time series based data, the model aims to incorporate embeddings that are fine-tuned on financial text along with a capacity to capture time based context. Experiments conducted on a dataset of financial stocks for a period from 2003 to 2020 help demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed RNN compared to other benchmark methods. It provides a result with 97% accuracy and accurately captures the context of verbal and time based sentiment context.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Models for Depression Prediction: A Comprehensive Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Millions of people across the globe suffer from depression, a common mental illness that needs to be diagnosed and treated early to avoid this from turning into something much serious. This paper aims at designing a system that predicts the likelihood of depression based on the structured questionnaire responses with the use of machine learning-based approach. The dataset is balanced with respect to the target classes "Depressed" and "Not Depressed" and comprises answers to 14 questions. Accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrices for five machine learning models were compared: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and an Artificial Neural Network (ANN). SVM performed the best in the contest of prediction accuracy and consistency by having an accuracy of 99% on testing.The proposed approach will prove to be a valuable asset for mental health professionals in allowing rapid and accurate depression screening. Future research will attempt to include larger datasets and explore more features in improving the robustness of prediction.

articleTitle: Identification of Cyber Bullying Using XGBoost Compared to Random Forest Classifier to Improve Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The study aims to improve the accuracy of cyberbullying detection. Compared to the Random Forest classifier, utilize XGBoost to improve accuracy. In this study, two groups were compared. The XGBoost Algorithm was compared in the study employing 1668 dataset samples, of which 573 were used for testing and 1554 for training. A sample size of 10 N was used for each in order to evaluate the detection of cyberbullying. The accuracy of the data is improved by the XGBoost with 94.416% and accuracy in comparison to Random Forest (87.703%). The detection of cyberbullying is statistically significant with a significant value of p=0.00192 (p<0.0496). Compared to Random Forest, the XGBoost Algorithm approach for detecting cyberbullying showed a notable improvement due to its increased accuracy.

articleTitle: Chicken Object Detection Using Faster Region-Based Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Monitoring chickens is important for managing health factors and assessing welfare. Increased infectious disease transmission brought on by increased poultry production can result in significant financial losses as well as widespread chicken mortality. Because of its non-invasive and invasive characteristics as well as its ability to display a wide range of information due to advancements in information technologies, computer vision can be trusted for the real-time automation of chicken health monitoring systems. Using a Faster Region-Based Convolutional Neural Network (Faster R-CNN) and sample images totaling 605 taken from poultry houses, this work introduces deeper learning to identify various breeds of chickens in the context of poultry. The best convolution architecture for real-time chicken detection was determined by testing and implementing three different convolutional architectures: ResNet-50, ResNet-101, and ResNeXt-101. Our findings show that we were more successful with Faster R-CNN in the context of ResNet-50. ResNet-50 was the most appropriate architecture to be implemented for real-world use in poultry management systems since, in spite of having more convolutional layers, its real-time processing time was quicker than ResNet-101's. The efficiency of ResNet-50 and Faster R-CNN has been used to monitor poultry more quickly and precisely.

articleTitle: Enhancing Out of Vocabulary(OOV) Token representation with Aggregated Conditional Random Fields model for Kannada NER
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Named entities are dynamic, as the contexts shift in a language, new entities emerge, reflecting the change over time, but large language models have a fixed vocabulary making it difficult to process out-of-vocabulary words(OOV), there are deep learning methods like BiLSTM, attention mechanism which can be used to get great results for Named entity recognition, but in case of low resource languages like Kannada, data available is not sufficient to train these deep learning models, so the research work attempts to solve the problem of NER using Aggregated Conditional Random Fields. The training is done on ai4bharat/naamapadam dataset which is the largest publicly available dataset for 11 major Indian languages including Kannada. The tokenization is done using a transformer-based multilingual model xlm-roberta-base. In this experiment, the OOV words are split into multiple sub-tokens and then aggregated using an additive pooling layer, and then passed on to the CRF classifier. Results show that the additive pooling model performs better than the base model benchmark and also better than vanilla CRF. Our model was able to produce an f1 score of 78.97 containing around 5728 OOV words in test and 14545 OOV words in the validation set.

articleTitle: Survey Paper: Comparative Analysis of Detection Methods for Real vs. AI-Generated Images
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The rapid evolution of AI-generated image technologies, including GANs and diffusion models, has blurred the lines between real and synthetic content. In this survey, we explore state-of-the-art methods for detecting fake images. Traditional forensic techniques, deep learning approaches, and advanced methods like Explainable AI (XAI) and blockchain-based verification are used. We evaluate these methods using performance metrics and derive insights into their strengths and limitations. A comparative analysis of existing research papers is provided, examining the approaches used, feature extraction techniques, classifiers employed, and datasets utilized. Additionally, it puts forth actional research directions like diffusion models, multimodal analysis, and expansion of dataset that can contribute towards the advancement of this field. Practical examples and visualizations make this survey both insightful and tutorial-like, offering valuable guidance for researchers and practitioners.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Techniques for Voice-Based Gender and Age Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This paper delves into deep learning approaches for gender and age prediction from voice data. We discuss a comparison of logistic regression and long short-term memory networks to predict gender, with Kmeans clustering along with logistic regression to predict the age of the speaker. In the obtained results, it is found that the LSTM model performs better than logistic regression in predicting the gender, we also compared it with machine learning models and Bayesian network and thus the hybrid approach successfully classifies the age groups. Some of these methods seem promising to be used in real-world applications in virtual assistants and healthcare.

articleTitle: Skin Cancer Detection using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Skin cancer becomes one of the various cancers most frequently diagnosed in most people around the globe; early diagnosis has always led to successful treatment. Deep learning techniques have shown to be useful for automated skin cancer detection from dermoscopic images. Here, we present a whole approach involving deep learning and machine learning features that can be used accurately for the efficient detection of skin cancer. We would work on building a highly functional deep learning model. The model would be trained on a large dataset of dermoscopic images that would feature various forms of skin lesions. Deep learning models, based on CNN technology, can capture minor features that present in an image; this therefore makes differentiation between malignant and benign lesions easier.

articleTitle: AI-Based Atrial Fibrillation Detection Using Pulse Rate Variability from PPG: A Comparative Study with HRV
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Atrial fibrillation is one of the most prevalent cardiac arrhythmias for an early diagnosis of its effective treatment. Traditionally, the diagnosis of AFib relies on Heart Rate Variability from electrocardiography. However, with the increase in accessibility of Photoplethysmography, Pulse Rate Variability derived from PPG may turn out to be the promising alternative to HRV. This paper investigates the diagnostic efficacy of PRV for AFib detection, comparing it to HRV using statistical analysis as well as several machine learning models. The dataset used is MIMIC-III PERform AF which comprises ECG and PPG recordings. Parameters related to HRV and PRV were calculated by extracting RR intervals from ECG signals and PP intervals from PPG signals. The similarity of HRV and PRV was analyzed through T-test and correlation. Machine learning models like Support Vector Machine SVM and Logistic Regression were trained on features of PRV to classify AFib and non-AFib cases. Results showed a high correlation between the two signals. High accuracy in the classification of AFib using PRV was obtained with machine learning models that were trained on PRV features, and Logistic Regression attained an accuracy of 98%. Results prove that PRV may be an alternative to HRV for AFib detection, especially in wearable applications, as a non-invasive low-cost solution.

articleTitle: Exploring the Effectiveness of Machine Learning Models in Detecting Anomalous Transactions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Money laundering and illicit financial flows facilitate criminal operations and undermine economic stability. Cryptocurrencies present regulatory challenges due to their anonymity and decentralized nature. Anomalous transactions refer to financial transactions that deviate from established patterns, indicating potential fraud, errors, or unusual behavior. This paper reviews machine learning techniques for detecting anomalous cryptocurrency transactions from an anti-money laundering/counter-terrorist financing (AML/CFT) perspective. A real-world Bitcoin transaction dataset is analyzed for our study. The paper assesses how well various machine learning models perform in detecting anomalous transactions. Detecting these anomalies is important in preventing fraud in areas like banking, e-commerce, and financial services.

articleTitle: Liver Disease Prediction Using Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Bayesian Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Liver illness is a great health concern worldwide, and the positive patient’s outcome relies on the early diagnosis. The body requires the liver to perform several vital functions. These functions include protein synthesis and digestion, as well as the storage and release of nutrients and wastes. This paper discusses how Bayesian network models, Deep learning, and Machine learning might improve the diagnosis of the liver disease. The Indian Liver Disease Patient Dataset (ILDPD) was used to test multiple models: Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Classifier, K-Nearest Neighbor, Gaussian NaiveBayes, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost, LightGBM, Bayesian Network, and ANN. Evaluation relies on accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and confusion matrix. ANN with 97.35% accuracy displayed the highest performance within all models in the study, which implies the more sophisticated Machine Learning and Deep Learning models can be the facilitators to expect the outcome of liver diseases. Neural networks, in particular, boost accuracy and cost-effectiveness of diagnosis.

articleTitle: Exploring Hybrid Approaches for Sentiment Classification: A Comparative Study of LSTM, Naive Bayes, and Bayesian Network on IMDB Reviews
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This paper evaluates the use of different types of models for machine learning and deep learning applied to sentiment analysis on the IMDb movie reviews dataset. Classical approaches, including Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression, and XGBoost, are compared with sequential deep architectures like (LSTM) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN). A Bayesian network is added to the portfolio in order to provide probabilistic inference for sentiment prediction. Techniques applied to preprocess the data include BoW and tokenization with padding. Results show that LSTM and RNN significantly identify sequential text patterns and perform well at high accuracy and F1 scores especially if input sequences are tokenized and padded. Classical models like Naive Bayes and Logistic Regression achieved competitive precision and recall capabilities with good computational efficiency and interpretability by using BoW features. XGBoost proved to be robust with optimized gradient-boosting techniques, while the Bayesian network presented a novel probabilistic approach, enabling the system to provide a probability of sentiment prediction based on the relationship between variables of sentiment and prediction. Results bring to light the potential integration of deep models with the capabilities of sequential learning and classical approaches or probabilistic models such as Bayesian networks for developing a scalable and efficient sentiment analysis framework for real-world applications. The experimental setup involves using LSTM, XGBoost, Naive Bayes, Logistic Regression and Bayesian Networks models to analyze IMDB movie reviews for sentiment classification has achieved 85.25, 86.13, 83, 90.21 and 80 accuracies respectively.

articleTitle: Credit Card Fraud Detection Utilizing Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Bayesian Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Detecting credit card fraud is a critical challenge in the modern financial landscape, where robust and efficient solutions are essential to mitigate losses and safeguard consumers. This research evaluates and contrasts three primary approaches to this issue: Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), and Bayesian Networks (BN). Using publicly available datasets, several ML techniques, including Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forests, Decision Trees, and XGBoost, were assessed alongside DL models such as Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and Deep Neural Networks (DNNs). Additionally, a Bayesian Network was employed to analyze causal relationships between fraud-related features, offering an interpretable probabilistic framework. While ML and DL approaches achieved high performance regarding accuracy, precision, and recall, the Bayesian Network distinguished itself by providing enhanced interpretability and reliability. This study highlights the complementary strengths of these methods and the potential for their integration to develop adaptive and efficient fraud detection systems

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Statistical Models on Credit Risk Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This study uses a dataset with several borrower characteristics to forecast credit risk using Machine learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) techniques in addition to statistical methods. With a 98.1% accuracy, the LGBM classifier outperformed the other models in this investigation and demonstrated the capacity to identify intricate risk patterns. The other machine learning models also shown outstanding performance; however, the statistical and deep learning frameworks were unable to achieve the same accuracy levels as machine learning methods. Sound lending practices and efficient risk management are enhanced by this multidimensional approach, which provides a wealth of information about the borrower's profile.

articleTitle: Enhanced Classification of Migraine Headaches: Leveraging Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Bayesian Networks with Data Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)

authors.preferredName: Arvapalli Venkata Naga Sai Hari Krishna

abstract: This study addresses the classification of migraine headaches using advanced machine learning techniques, specifically ensemble models and boosting methods. We employed data augmentation to enhance a dataset of 400 samples to 1449, ensuring balanced class distribution. Our approach leverages Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest (RF), k-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Decision Trees (DT), Deep Neural Networks (DNN), and Bayesian Network. The results demonstrate significant improvements in classification accuracy, with the best-performing models achieving up to 99.66% accuracy. This research contributes to the field by showcasing the effectiveness of combining data augmentation with advanced machine learning techniques for improved migraine classification.

articleTitle: Heart Disease Risk Assessment using Bayesian Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This paper uses Bayesian Networks to display an extensive approach to heart disease risk assessment. Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are one of the main leading causes of death worldwide, making up 32% of all global fatalities [1]. We developed and analyzed different types of Bayesian Network models to predict and estimate the risk of heart disease based on patient data [8]. Our approach includes domain knowledge, structure learning algorithms, and feature selection techniques to create an accurate and understandable model. The final model achieves an ROC AUC score of 0.846, displaying its capability in risk prediction. We also explore practical applications of the model for medical decision support [2].

articleTitle: Detection of Forged Handwritten Signatures Using Deep Architectures
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Detecting forged handwritten signatures is essential for maintaining the security of authentication systems in various fields. This study leverages Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and an upgraded transfer learning model, MobileNet, to enhance the accuracy of signature forgery detection. The research begins with a CNN-based model and later integrates MobileNet for improved performance. The Kaggle "Handwritten Signatures" dataset was utilized, with data augmentation and early stopping applied to optimize training. The results demonstrate that MobileNet significantly outperforms the baseline CNN model, achieving high accuracy and robustness in identifying forged signatures.

articleTitle: Integration of Biomechanical Sensor in Spinal Brace for Posture Detection and Correction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Over the past decade, 60% of people have been affected by spinal curvature at some point in their lives. It is a disease of the spine bones such as kyphosis, lordosis, and scoliosis that affects humans and occurs most commonly in adults, although the cause of most childhood cases is unknown. Everyone has some degree of curvature, but when it exceeds about certain degrees, it causes turbulence and difficulty breathing. It is diagnosed by methods such as X-rays and other measurements. It is treated using a variety of techniques, such as Back support requires less adjustment and is more comfortable. This may cause back pain, injury, and ventilation insufficiency for the person wearing the brace. The main goal of our research is to develop a spinal brace with circuits to detect the biomechanical properties of the spine in order to develop innovative and improved functions. The proposed system used for detection spinal curvature angle using biomechanical sensors like IMU and flex sensors. The sensor data is processed by NodeMCU so that the data can be compared with real-time data. When a difference is detected, a signal is passed to a vibrator and it begin alert. Furthermore, the system enhances the automatic correction with pressure cuff mechanism. The developed system overcome the disadvantages of traditional construction methods and proposes a model with high flexibility, strength, durability, and breathability. The system is resulting in less pain, better ventilation, and increased comfort and adjustability. The conclusion marks that the system has better efficiency and effectiveness in usage, which made bridge between gap of clinical and remote assessment

articleTitle: AyurMate: Blending Ayurveda and Artificial Intelligence for Personalized Wellness
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: AyurMate is an advanced chatbot that utilizes AI to offer tailored advice based on the Ayurvadic perspective. As more people around the world seek complete Ayurvedic healthcare, AyurMate harmonizes ancient medical systems with contemporary technological advancements to ensure effective health strategies are both available and convenient.Using deep learning frameworks like Keras and NLP tools like NLTK, AyurMate does a great job of classifying the way a user utilizes the application and suggesting the most appropriate Ayurvedic treatment. This is made possible by a well-structured ANN model that accurately predicts the user’s demands based on the desired intents and responses dataset. The chatbot addresses health issues such as fever, indigestion, skin troubles and many others.AyurMate’s versatile architecture incorporates the chatAI interface into Flask for deployment purposes, enabling real-time communication with users. This paper presents its design, implementation, and applications by stating its significance in enhancing the access of Ayurvedic medicine in terms of wider adoption of the traditional field in AI technologies.

articleTitle: Automated Traffic Light Control System for Ambulance Using Laser Signals and Raspberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Urban traffic congestion poses a major challenge, particularly for emergency services like ambulances, where delays can have life-threatening consequences. This paper proposes a novel, cost-efficient Automated Traffic Light Control System aimed at prioritizing ambulances at busy intersections, thereby reducing delays and ensuring faster response times. The system utilizes Raspberry Pi Zero 2W, Laser Diodes (KY-008), and Light Dependent Resistors (LDRs) to detect ambulances and dynamically control traffic lights. Unlike traditional systems relying on GPS or RFID technologies, this laser-based approach offers greater precision and affordability through the use of modulated laser signals. Experimental results reveal that this system reduces ambulance response times by 35%. The tests were conducted under simulated urban conditions, highlighting the system's capability to outperform conventional solutions. The simplicity of integration and real-time responsiveness underscore its potential for widespread urban adoption.

articleTitle: Detection of Drones using Acoustic Signals and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Drone detection using radar is popular. Diffraction effect of the signal is the main challenge in radar-based detection. An alternative approach to address the diffraction effect is acoustic signals. In this work, acoustic based detection of drones is proposed. Various possibilities of drones are single rotor, multi rotor, fixed wing, nano, medium, large and heavy lift. Acoustic signals are different for various types of drones. Features from acoustic signals are integrated with machine learning algorithms. Pitch features are important in audio signals. Hence, in this paper pitch and other features are explored to detect drones. To classify the drones, Decision Tree and Support Vector Machine based Machine Learning algorithms are explored. It is easy to detect drones using acoustic signals instead of radio frequencies, cameras, and radars. Performance of the proposed methods are assessed using confusion matrix.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Medical Imaging Interface for Lung Disease Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This paper discusses a novel approach for classifying lung diseases using multi-modal medical imaging techniques. By integrating data from various imaging modalities such as X-ray, CT scan, and MRI, our model aims to improve accuracy and reliability in disease diagnosis. Through advanced Deep learning algorithms and feature extraction methods, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in accurately identifying and classifying different types of lung diseases, ultimately contributing to more precise and efficient patient care. Furthermore, we introduce an innovative enhancement to our approach through the integration of Grad-CAM (Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping) technology. This augmentation enables the generation of heatmaps that highlight regions of interest in medical images, providing insights into the severity and localization of abnormalities associated with lung diseases. By incorporating Grad-CAM, our model not only facilitates accurate disease classification but also offers clinicians valuable visual aids for assessing disease severity and planning treatment strategies. Combining the power of Python with the flexibility of PyQt, our application aims to provide a user-friendly interface for various tasks. Through careful design and implementation, we demonstrate the seamless integration of PyQt widgets, layouts, and functionalities to create an intuitive and efficient desktop application. This application serves as a valuable tool for healthcare professionals, enabling them to leverage our advanced classification model and Grad-CAM technology in a user-friendly manner, ultimately enhancing the quality and efficiency of patient care.

articleTitle: Frame-Level Audio Hate Speech Detection for Kannada Language
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Detecting hate speech in audio has become increasingly challenging due to the increasing use of internet platforms and digital communication. Through this study, we develop an audio-based speech classifier to facilitate the detection of hate speech in the Kannada language. We present an approach to classifying hate speech at the frame level by extracting audio features such as Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs), spectral bandwidth, spectral contrast, and chroma features. Furthermore, we present a custom Kannada hate speech dataset to address the scarcity of resources for hate speech studies in the Kannada language. We collected over 40 minutes of audio samples from YouTube and X (formerly Twitter). Our experiments show that an optimized XGBoost model achieved an accuracy of 73% on the custom dataset for frame-level classification. We also propose a cascading classifiers approach with two classifiers to exploit the locality of hate speech that improves the accuracy to 77%. Finally, we benchmark the proposed model against Logistic Regression, SVM, and XGBoost models.

articleTitle: Predicting Sevearity of Type 2 Diabetic Retinopathy Using Retinal Fundus Images with new DeepLearning Architectures from the Inception and Resnet Families
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Due to its high morbidity and medical expenses, DR mellitus (T2DM) is a serious global health concern. Its burden can be lessened with effective early prognosis, but the available treatments are not enough. Predictive modelling of Retina Images (fundus) can enhance early diagnosis and care quality. Advanced convolutional neural networks (Inception-V4, ResNet V1, and ResNet V2) are used in this study to assess the severity of Diabetic Retinopathy caused by T2DM. Using de-identified fundus data from 9,948 individuals (1,904 with a T2DM diagnosed), we used transfer learning to train these models. We have performed simple data augmentation to rectify the class imbalance. The accuracy and AUC of the ensemble model were 94.21% and 98.53%, respectively. The findings imply that the combination of ResNet and Inception-V4 enhances classification power, providing a viable approach for early T2DM identification from fundus data that may find use in clinical settings. Future research still needs to focus on improving sensitivity and integrating real-time.

articleTitle: Leveraging Insights from KNN and LSTM Models for Alzheimer’s Disease Early Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: In this research, soft computing methods are explored for the early detection of dementia from EEG signal analysis. The study extract features from key frequency bands (Delta, Theta, Alpha, Beta) and uses the machine learning models such as K Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) networks to identify small cognitive changes. Specifically, the LSTM model exhibits exceptional performance, particularly with increased sensitivity and specificity, especially in the Alpha and Beta bands, for early stage dementia detection. This work provides a promising alternate to costly existing methods and contributes to the development of noninvasive, scalable diagnostic tools for dementia. Early detection by observing the synchrony across the brain lobe could help improve diagnosis and contribute to future AI based healthcare applications.

articleTitle: Inorganic Chemical Reaction Predictor Using Random Forest and Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The Chemical Reaction Predictor project shall use machine learning approaches to make predictions on chemical reaction effects. When a large enough group of known reactions is available, each identified set of reactants and products can be used to construct a model into which can be fed any set of reactants. It includes data acquisition and data pre-processing, feature selection of reactant properties and reaction conditions, and construction of several predictive models. The first and main goal is to dogmatically apply machine learning models such as Random Forests and Support Vector Machines to attain an accuracy of 60% or higher. Furthermore, we measure the accuracy, and other measures such as precision, recall, and F1 score to determine the efficiency of these models. Finally, while the optimal model is found and implemented, it is brought within a simple graphical user interface that enables the users to input reactants and obtain predicted products.

articleTitle: Personalized Re-Ranking of Universities and Colleges Using NIRF and JoSAA Data
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) provides a comprehensive evaluation of colleges across India based on various parameters such as teaching, learning, resources, research, and outreach. It integrates these parameters by giving a fixed priority to each of them. In today’s competitive academic landscape, choosing the right college is a crucial decision for students seeking higher education. This depends on several factors specific to each student such as their social background, location, economic status and rank in the qualifying examination, etc.This research introduces a novel approach to enhance the utility of NIRF data by creating user-specific rankings tailored to individual preferences. By incorporating user-defined criteria such as median salary, number of students placed, facilities for Physically Challenged Students (PCS), faculty strength, research funding, the proposed system generates personalized rankings that align with the unique needs and aspirations of each student.Our system utilizes a novel skyline-based approach and analyzes the NIRF data alongside user preferences to generate dynamic rankings that adapt to evolving student priorities. We show multiple use-cases to demonstrate the utility of our approach in real-world scenarios, and study the way colleges are ranked for different user preferences. Our study shows that the college rankings so obtained can be quite different from the standard NIRF ranking.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Classifier for Human Daily Activities
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Human action recognition system using wearable sensors for classification of human daily activities is presented. Data collected for six daily human activities using smart phone with the help of thirty subjects is used. Thirteen time domain and two frequency domain features are extracted from the sensor data. Two machine learning algorithms namely decision tree and support vector machine and one deep learning algorithm LSTM is used for classification. The performance of the three classifiers in classifying the daily activities is evaluated using the performance metrics precision, specificity, recall, f-score and accuracy. Simulation results shows that the overall accuracy of SVM is 99.30% which is 2.88% and 0.53% higher than decision tree and LSTM respectively.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence keeps women safe: Preventing online and domestic Violence
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Currently, emerging artificial intelligence is revolutionizing global practices by addressing the most alarming factors in the world, mainly raising female security against urgent needs. This report highlights how AI can provide input for the identification of domestic violence by early signs of harassment or even signs related to cyberbullying. From these predictive models, analyzing behavior, language, or any interaction, AI predicts instances showing the presence of abuse by having enough time to take preemption. This study provides the conceptual grounds of AI for protecting women further to the application of the research in monitoring abusive online-based activities and alerting users and corresponding authorities. Therefore, this paper shows the depth of impact of AI on women's safety and how technology can emerge from ideas to practical application. This research study, therefore, brings cutting-edge innovations in AI to societal awareness and action by demonstrating AI's potential to create a safer, more equitable world for women, both online and offline.

articleTitle: An Evaluation Metric for Assessing Summary-Level Semantic Similarity in Abstractive Text Summarization
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Abstractive text summarization focuses on producing summaries that retain the most critical information from the original document. ROUGE is a widely used metric for evaluating summarization quality. However, it relies solely on comparing n-grams between the generated and reference summaries. To overcome this limitation, this paper introduces a semantic similarity-based evaluation metric. Unlike ROUGE, the proposed approach evaluates summaries by assessing the similarity between system-generated and reference summaries using cosine similarity between their sentence embeddings. When evaluating the abstractive summaries on the ROUGE and the proposed evaluation metric, it is observed that the latter has a stronger correlation with human judgment.

articleTitle: Comparative study of various machine learning model in Prediction of Parkinson’s Disease
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that shows prominent features of motor symptoms, such as tremor, rigidity, and bradykinesia, along with many important non-motor symptoms. Although early diagnosis and monitoring are tricky due to the lack of definite biomarkers in PD, most patients typically show specific vocal characteristics, and thus voice recordings can be an encouraging non-invasive approach for early detection and monitoring. In this study, various vocal features-based machine learning models will be applied and compared for the prediction of PD. This comparative study would involve several machine learning models like logistic regression, Support Vector Machines (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), decision trees, random forests, and neural networks. The database used was obtained from the UCI Machine Learning Repository. This consisted of biomedical voice measures made for 31 subjects, out of which 23 were patients with PD. In total, there were 195 voice recordings labeled as healthy or affected with PD. Among the models tested, the KNN model reached an accuracy as high as 96.61% and with a perfect recall at 100%. The SVM model had a perfect precision and specificity, both at 100%, but an accuracy as high as 93.26%.

articleTitle: Real-time Brain Stroke Detection using CT Scans
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Brain stroke is a serious medical condition that requires timely and accurate diagnosis to save lives and reduce long-term complications. In this study, we explore how deep learning can be applied to classify brain CT scans into two categories: stroke and normal. We evaluated four cutting edge convolutional neural network architectures—DenseNetl21, VGG16, VGG19, and ResNet50 and found DenseNetl21 to be the most effective, achieving an impressive test accuracy of 98.63%. To notice the challenge of class imbalance in the dataset, we used data augmentation approaches, which improved model’s training and generalization capabilities. These findings underscore DenseNetl21’s potential to deliver precise and efficient stroke detection, paving the way for its use in real-time clinical settings. Moving forward, our research will focus on localizing stroke affected regions, classifying different stroke subtypes, and implementing the model in diverse clinical environments to enhance diagnostic workflows.

articleTitle: Peer to Peer Money Lending Using Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: In recent times, the fusion of blockchain technology and peer-to-peer lending has emerged as a transformative force in finance. This synergy offers a decentralized and transparent alternative to conventional lending, empowering individuals and businesses to access credit directly. While promising greater inclusivity, this approach also confronts challenges like trust issues and borrower risk assessment. To confront these hurdles, this paper aims to harness blockchain and machine learning to forge a more secure and efficient peer-to-peer lending ecosystem. The paper pioneers an innovative paradigm in peer-to-peer lending, merging blockchain technology and advanced machine learning algorithms. It seeks to deploy blockchain based smart contracts to streamline lending transactions, cutting out intermediaries and bolstering security. Additionally, it aims to integrate machine learning for robust borrower authentication and risk evaluation. By leveraging extensive borrower data and historical patterns, the system intends to generate reliable credit scores, facilitating informed lending decisions and risk mitigation.

articleTitle: Speech Emotion Recognition using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Emotion recognition from speech is an emerging field within machine learning, aimed at improving human-computer interaction by enabling systems to understand and respond to human emotions. This paper presents a comprehensive study on Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) using machine learning techniques. We explore various feature extraction methods, including Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCCs) and chroma features, to capture the emotional content from speech signals. The extracted features are utilized to train several machine learning models, including Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forests, and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Our approach is evaluated on publicly available datasets, and the performance is assessed using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. The experimental results demonstrate that our proposed models achieve significant improvements in emotion classification accuracy compared to existing methods. Additionally, we discuss the challenges and potential applications of SER in real-world scenarios, such as customer service, mental health monitoring, and virtual assistants. The findings of this study contribute to the advancement of robust and efficient SER systems, paving the way for more empathetic and intuitive human-computer interactions..

articleTitle: A Survey on Vehicle Collision Avoidance Systems: Innovations, Challenges, and Future Prospects
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Vehicle Collision Avoidance Systems (VCAS) enhance road safety by enabling vehicles to autonomously detect and respond to potential hazards using technologies such as radar, LiDAR, cameras, V2X communication, and machine learning algorithms. Key features like Adaptive Cruise Control, Autonomous Emergency Braking, and Lane Departure Warning help prevent accidents and improve driver assistance. Despite challenges like sensor limitations in adverse conditions, communication delays, and cybersecurity risks, advancements in sensor accuracy, decision-making algorithms, and edge computing continue to drive innovation. This paper highlights the importance of technological improvements, regulatory frameworks, and system interoperability in advancing VCAS adoption and achieving safer, autonomous transportation.

articleTitle: Diabetic Foot Ulcer Detection Using Deep Learning: A Focus on EfficientNet for Enhanced Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers is a common side effect of diabetes.A DFU is a critical condition that can lead to the amputation of a diabetic patient’s lower limb.Early diagnosis thus becomes very critical.The occurrence of diabetes complications can be linked to a lack of information among diabetes patients, who are often unaware of the negative consequences of their illness.In light of this, the study suggests using the EfficientNet deep neural network model for diabetic foot ulcer prediction.Around 500 photos of healthy and the diabetic ulcer-affected patients’ feet are used to train the EfficientNet model. The depth, breadth, and picture resolution levels are the three distinct characteristics on which the network processing takes place.By combining the input image’s depth, width, and resolution and using fewer parameters, EfficientNet has outperformed earlier methods. The EfficientNet model outperformed well-known models including AlexNet and VGG. It gave maximum testing acuraccy of 100%.These result suggest that EfficientNet is a reliable tool for early DFU detection, potentially reducing the risk of amputations in diabetic patients.

articleTitle: Visualizing Network Traffic Data for Cybersecurity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Network traffic analysis is essential to ensuring strong cybersecurity in today's digital environment. The growing volume and complexity of network traffic frequently proves too much for traditional network monitoring systems, which rely on manual log checks and simple visualizations. The efficiency of cybersecurity defenses may be jeopardized by these restrictions, which may cause delays in identifying and reacting to security attacks. The goal of this project is to create a sophisticated and scalable visualization tool especially for network traffic analysis in cybersecurity settings. The main objective is to develop real-time, high-performance visualizations that can process and show vast amounts of network traffic data. This solution will assist cybersecurity experts in detecting possible risks, identifying abnormalities, and responding to incidents more efficiently by utilizing interactive visualizations and powerful data processing algorithms. In order to improve anomaly detection, boost real-time processing, and increase the precision of threat identification, future improvements will concentrate on integrating machine learning and statistical techniques. In dynamic and changing network settings, this study lays the groundwork for more effective and responsive cybersecurity defenses.

articleTitle: Enhanced Telecom Customer Churn Prediction Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Customer churn prediction is the greatest priority for telecom companies wishing to retain their customers and minimize revenue loss. Thus, in this paper, several machine learning and deep learning models have been used for predicting the churn of telecom customers. These include the Random Forest, Logistic Regression, AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting, and Deep Neural Networks (DNN). In doing so, an emphasis was placed on feature selection, data preprocessing, and class balancing within the text, using the Kaggle Telecom Customer Churn dataset. The presented results highlight the accuracy enhancement abilities of ensemble learning and DNNs while performing experiments at different metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Furthermore, it also highlights the point of interpretability and understanding churning behavior in telecom settings by deploying predictive models in real-world telecom settings.

articleTitle: Credit Card Fraud Detection using Machine learning algorithms and Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Credit card fraud detection is a crucial domain where the identification of complex patterns in transaction data is paramount. Deep learning, particularly Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs), offers advanced techniques to enhance the detection, prevention, and mitigation of fraudulent activities. However, existing methods for credit card fraud detection often fail to incorporate essential features that reflect realistic fraudulent behavior. This research focuses on the developing an ANN model and compares it with other popular machine learning models to detect credit card fraud and help users stay protected. The ANN model was optimized to handle the challenges of class imbalance and the sparse nature of fraud instances, ensuring robustness and reliability. When compared to other models in the domain of credit card fraud detection, our ANN model demonstrates a clear advantage in terms of accuracy and robustness with an accuracy of 99.99%.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Framework for Accident Detection and Risk Assessment Using CNN and Graph-Based Analytics
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This proposed work introduces a comprehensive accident detection and risk assessment system that coordinate the strengths of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and a graph-based analytical approach. With support of YOLOv8, deep learning model for object detection, the system perform real-time identification vehicles, pedestrians, and other road entities from video feeds, such as CCTV footage and user-generated videos. This detection capability is integrated with a graph-based model that represents these entities as nodes and their interactions as edges. The proximity, trajectory, and relative speeds of the entities are analyzed to assess collision risk dynamically. The combined approach enhances the system’s ability to identify potential accidents and evaluate risk levels with high precision. The CNN component ensures accurate object detection and classification, while the graph-based analysis facilitates real-time spatial reasoning and interaction assessment. A user-friendly web interface enables real-time visualization of detections and risk analyses, supporting collaboration with traffic authorities and urban planners. This approach not only aids in accident detection but also provides actionable insights for proactive risk mitigation and traffic management.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Various Machine Learning Techniques for Diabetes Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Diabetes is a pervasive chronic disease affecting millions worldwide, necessitating effective and early prediction to improve patient outcomes and reduce healthcare costs. This study presents a comparative analysis of various machine learning models in prediction of diabetes, with an emphasis on both individual model performance and ensemble methods. Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Decision Tree, Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors, and XGBoost model’s performance are analyzed using a dataset of clinical health indicators. Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-score are the key metrics considered to determine their predictive model performance. Furthermore, a Voting Classifier is implemented to explore whether an ensemble of models can outperform individual algorithms in terms of predictive accuracy and robustness.Outcomes of the experimental results indicate that the XGBoost model and the Voting Classifier provide superior accuracy and reliability, making them effective tools for early-stage diabetes prediction. This research highlights the potential of machine learning in healthcare and suggests a promising approach to predictive modeling for diabetes diagnosis.

articleTitle: Advances in Image Analysis: Leveraging Computer Vision for Automated Recognition and Interpretation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Computer vision has revolutionized image analysis by enabling automated recognition and interpretation of complex visual data. This study delves into recent advancements in deep learning, focusing on convolutional neural networks (CNNs), attention mechanisms, and comparative evaluations with newer architectures such as Vision Transformers and EfficientDet. Using datasets such as ImageNet, COCO, and NIH Chest X-ray, our model demonstrated a 20% improvement in classification accuracy compared to YOLOv5 and a 12% improvement over EfficientDet on medical imaging tasks. Strategies to address challenges like occlusion, lighting variability, and false positives are discussed. Our findings highlight significant improvements in classification accuracy, object detection precision, and computational efficiency, paving the way for scalable and real-time applications in healthcare, autonomous systems, and industrial automation.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Air Quality Forecasting Using Machine and Deep Learning Based Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Many emerging nations are experiencing severe air pollution on account of the growing urbanization and industry. Because air pollution has an impact on global human health and sustainable development, governments and it is becoming source of concern in society. Anticipating air pollution thus became essential. Prediction of air quality has gained popularity by virtue of the volume and a range of data that air quality surveillance systems have collected. This paper uses a Python framework to analyze the air quality, implementing historical air quality data analysis for Bangalore city and predicting its quality exercising a number of machine and deep learning (D-Learning) models. In the proposed work, 5 distinct Machine learning(M-Learning) models including Random Forest regression (RFR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Linear regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), and Long Short- Term Model of D-Learning Technique (D-LSTM) have been accustomed to compute the Air Quality Index (AQI) of Bangalore city. This strategy has been put into practice in Google Collab with GPU run time. As stated by the measures including Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), D-Learning- based LSTM model has demonstrated better reliability than other M-Learning models. Performance metrics values for LSTM is superior compared to the rest of M-Learning models

articleTitle: Comprehensive Deep Learning Framework For Diabetic Retinopathy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy is one of the foremost attractions to impaired vision across the world and especially in working-age adults. While still among the major reasons for distorted vision worldwide and more so among working-age adults, diabetic retinopathy, without having any early detection, is responsible for some of the most severe forms of blindness. Such fields in coastal Karnataka, India, where the art of retinal fundus imaging still lacks technical knowledge, experience, and skills, might have been able to avert such outermost disasters of patients. The mission aims closer to the development of a deep learning model to create an automated class framework that generates the DR stage, i.e. moderate, mild, severe, and proliferative retinopathy, from fundus pictures. One of the core architecture models noted to be very efficient while analyzing medical images is the CNN. Some data preprocessing techniques also enhance the performance which includes resizing, normalization, and augmentation. This classification process is performed in three phases: first with real-time data, second with the publicly available dataset on Kaggle, and then the combination of real-time as well as Kaggle images to further classify. These phases are compared in terms of performance metrics, such as accuracy, precision, and recall with cross-validation. This project has the potential to revolutionize diabetic eye care by offering speedy and accurate DR classification.

articleTitle: Multibody Kinematics of Prosthetic Arm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This paper shows the kinematic imitations of the robot arm that can simulate a human arm and wrist. This robotic arm can be analyzed by the changes in the torque needed to be unleashed and the changes in velocity that travel by the fingertip end positioning through three-dimensional space. It is necessary to simulate multiple robotics phenomena. An implementation through MATLAB with SIMSCAPE uses a sinusoidal harmonic wave as a motion input, and the power is calculated automatically. This motion in X, Y, and Z directions gives an understanding of the end effector’s movement through velocity profile graphs; it is a simulation model-eye candy manifestation. Transformation methods in multibody dynamics are explored to simulate the same robotic arm to verify that this is how the engineering design and operational efficiencies should look. The results show that arm movements were effective since the basis is put down here for further torque optimization and structural design. This proposed method is adaptable for the future for potential simulation in robotic systems of link-joint operators and therefore may become an important tool to potentially advocate and model advanced robotic systems for their application in prosthetics among other imperative functionalities.

articleTitle: Detection of Brain Tumor Using a Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This study introduces a deep learning-based method for classifying brain tumors using a pre-trained VGG19 convolutional neural network (CNN). By leveraging transfer learning, we adapted the VGG19 model with custom fully connected layers and trained it on MRI images to differentiate between tumor and non-tumor cases. The model’s architecture includes dropout layers to minimize overfitting and enhance generalization while maintaining the robust feature extraction capabilities of the VGG19 base. We developed a Flask web application interface to make the model accessible via web-based user input, allowing users to upload MRI images and receive immediate predictions on tumor presence. Preliminary results show that proposed model can accurately classify brain tumor images with high accuracy, highlighting the potential of deep learning in automating brain tumor diagnostics. This tool could significantly aid clinicians in making rapid and accurate diagnoses, ultimately improving patient outcomes.

articleTitle: Lip Reading Detection Using Convolution Neural Network and Recurrent Neural Network with LSTM
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Speech recognition system that has fused computer vision with deep learning to recognize spoken words with excellent accuracy. This model uses Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) units to simulate temporal relationships in the speech sequence and 3D Convolu- tional Neural Networks (3D CNN) to extract spatial and temporal characteristics from video inputs, such as lip movements. Even in challenging settings, the capabilities of combining audio-visual information allow the system to collect essential knowledge and ensure that successful recognition is warranted. TensorFlow and Keras libraries are utilized when implementing the suggested architecture, whose performance is marvelous with a 98.5% validation accuracy and 95.7% training accuracy. This technique shows how computer vision and deep learning can be combined to improve the precision and resilience of speech recognition systems.

articleTitle: Comparison of Novel Long Short-Term Memory Over Recurrent Neural Networks for Predicting the Melting Pattern of Ice in Antarctic Sea Based on Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Revolutionary technique that blends revolutionary Novel Long Short-Term Memory (NLSTM) with Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), this research seeks to revolutionize the prediction of ice melting. This research paper's dataset, which has 212 rows and 3 columns (attributes), was obtained from Kaggle.com. This has to do with Antarctic mass, year, and 1-sigma uncertainty. The clincalc web application was utilized to determine a total sample size of 92 for the paper. Gpower sets a value of α=0.05 and power=0.80 to find a sample size of 20 for each group. Based on the data obtained from the two groups NLSTM has a much greater accuracy (98.64%) as compared to that of RNN accuracy (96.78%). Statistical significance was noted between NLSTM and RNN with p = 0.002 (Independent Sample T-Test, p < 0.05). In summary, the research indicates that the NLSTM outperforms the RNN in terms of accuracy in which the Climate in Change Factor dataset is used.

articleTitle: Comparision of Principal Component Analysis, K-means, and Generative Adversarial Network for Compression and reconstruction of medical image
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Medical images are essential in healthcare, but their large file sizes present challenges for storage and transmission. This study proposes a framework for compressing color medical images while preserving key visual information. We apply three compression models: Principal Component Analysis (PCA), K-Means clustering, and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), and evaluate their performance based on Compression Ratio (CR), Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and Structural Similarity Index (SSIM). K-Means with 100 clusters outperforms the other models, achieving the highest compression (CR of 1.20), with excellent image quality (PSNR of 66.77 dB, SSIM of 1.0000). PCA shows moderate performance with a CR of 2.45, while GAN provides the least effective compression and image quality. These results demonstrate that K-Means offers the best trade-off between compression and image fidelity.

articleTitle: Capsule Networks for COVID-19 Detection with Explainable AI via Grad-CAM
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: In recent years, the world has faced a severe epidemic, COVID-19, which has significantly impacted global health. Traditional laboratory methods for COVID-19 detection are time-consuming and likely to make errors. Early and Accurate detection can save lives. The urgent need for early detection of this life-threatening disease has driven the designing of advanced AI techniques to detect COVID-19. Even though advanced AI models have been developed for COVID-19 detection, they lack explanation regarding the model’s decisions. The use of explainable models is essential to support clinical decision-making systems. This research develops a methodology to overcome these challenges of time-consuming disease prediction and lack of explainable AI models. We propose a Capsule Network with a customized dynamic routing algorithm, combined with an explainable AI technique using Grad-CAM, to enhance the efficiency of detection of COVID-19 in chest X-rays. Grad-CAM visualizations highlight relevant regions in chest X-rays, providing critical insights to support the decision system of the proposed model. The proposed model achieved a test accuracy of 99.64%, training accuracy of 99.47%, recall of 99%, 100% precision, 99% F1-score, and AUC scores of 99.54% and 99.89% on training and testing data, respectively. The integration of explainability methods offers a valuable tool for medical professionals, improving the reliability and transparency of AI-driven diagnoses.

articleTitle: Smart Locker 2.0: Leveraging IoT and Machine Learning for Secure, User-Friendly Public Storage
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Smart locker systems are a revolutionary technology, combining advanced automation and connectivity to address increasingly demanding requirements for secure, efficient, and convenient storage solutions in numerous scenarios. These intelligent lockers use the latest technologies, such as the Internet of Things (IoT) and mobile applications, to revolutionize the way people store their belongings. Existing Smart Locker System lacks measurable results. To sustain its claims, we include key findings. For security, the system utilizes RFID authentication and biometric security, which reduces unauthorized access by 98% and blocks spoofing attacks. For convenience, a study with 50 users found 92% satisfaction, with 87% preferring it over traditional lockers due to faster access, averaging 3 seconds. For environmental benefits, the system cut power use by using sleep mechanism and saved paper usage by switching to cloud logs. Real-World tests achieved 98% user satisfaction with the university system proving its efficiency, security, and sustainability. This system expounds on multifaceted benefits and functionalities in smart lockers. First, it covers how these lockers provide better security compared to old lock-and-key systems. Using access controls reduces the risk of theft and illegal access to one's valuables and sensitive belongings by a great degree. It has an easy reservation, access, and management of personal lockers via a remote means; this proves to be seamless without needing any physical keys and contactless interactions, ideal for modern spaces considering hygiene and efficiency is top priority. Moreover, it goes on to analyze the flexibility of smart locker systems. From corporate offices to co-working spaces, universities, shopping malls, and public transportation hubs, these lockers cater to diverse user needs, creating flexible and scalable solutions adaptable to a variety of environments.

articleTitle: Exploring LSTM vs. BERT for Event Detection in Social Media Posts
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: In today’s digital world, social media and online platforms generate a lot of unstructured text data. Event detection and classification from such data becomes important for understanding and responding to global events. Classifying text into categories like political events, riots, and disasters plays a important role in public safety, disaster response, and media analysis. This work compares the performance of LSTM and BERT, on a event classification task to categorize social media posts into five event categories: terror, political, disaster, riot, and positive. The results indicate that BERT outperforms LSTM in all the evaluating metrics. LSTM generally delivers more balanced but less accurate results, often with a faster processing time. In cases where precision is crucial, models like BERT are preferred, even if they require higher computational resources. This work tells importance of selecting a model that goes along with the specific demands of task complexity and available computational resources.

articleTitle: Personalized Predictive Healthcare Using Machine Learning and Generative AI
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: In the modern world, the convergence of technology and healthcare presents an opportunity to deliver individualized and reasonably priced health support at the user’s fingertips. This study offers a system that can serve as a personal health assistant by providing comprehensive health insights and early disease prediction. In order to predict possible health issues, users provide three primary symptoms and basic biographical information like age and gender. Using a voting ensemble model, the system generates a final prediction by integrating predictions from seven machine learning models: decision trees, random forests, naive bayes, logistic regression, SVM, K-nearest neighbors, and XGBoost. The system combines generative AI with predictive analytics to provide comprehensive explanations of the anticipated disease, including causes, symptoms, solutions, and available treatments. The generative AI model gives information that is tailored to each user’s needs by considering factors like age and gender. Evaluation measures that demonstrate the system’s efficacy and dependability include accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. By providing easily available health insights, this user-friendly platform raises awareness and makes it easier for people to make educated health decisions.

articleTitle: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Evaluation Framework for Question Answering System
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Question-answering (QA) systems have become crucial in healthcare, decision-making, finance, and research domains. While transformer-based language models have greatly enhanced the generation of contextually relevant answers, they often struggle to provide reliable answers, leading to hallucinations and incorrect predictions. Traditional evaluation metrics, such as exact match, precision, recall, and F1 metric, demonstrate significant limitations in comprehensively assessing the performance and capabilities of QA systems. This research introduces a commonsense reasoning-based evaluation framework for language models, leveraging the Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning approach. Our proposed method integrates CoT reasoning with a GPT o1-mini model to evaluate the predictions from language models. Experiments conducted on the SQuAD 2.0 dataset demonstrate significant improvements in handling the answers generated by the language models and increase the reliability of the QA system. The framework offers robust and interpretable solutions, addressing critical gaps in current QA systems and ensuring reliability and transparency for practical, real-world applications.

articleTitle: Bayesian-Driven Deep Learning and Machine Learning Approaches for Handwritten Word Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Identifying handwritten words poses a complicated problem owing to the variances in handwriting styles and the possible noise and distortions present in the data. The performance of used deep learning and traditional machine learning handwriting recognition methods for recognizing handwritten words is studied in this paper and the advantages of using deep learning are discussed. In particular, neural network models such as CNN and 2DLSTM networks had a great work in this area. In contrast, we detect whole handwritten words without the need of segments into standalone characters. The CNNs are used for feature extraction, the Bidirectional LSTMs for sequence prediction and output is decoded via a CTC layer. The model was evaluated over the IAM words dataset from the IAM handwriting database, achieving 87% accuracy and a character error rate of 7.77%. In addition, we experimented with ML techniques, including SVM, RF has got an accuracy of 72% and 80% accuracies, and a Bayesian network of 61% accuracy, to provide a comparative analysis.

articleTitle: Improving accuracy in Text Extraction From images using Region-Based Convolutional Neural Networks algorithm compared to Convolutional Neural Network algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Text extraction is a critical task in data processing and analysis, requiring high accuracy for effective applications. This research employed a publicly accessible Kaggle dataset to assess the performance of two neural network architectures that are Region-Based Convolutional Neural Networks (R-CNN) with that of standard Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). A total sample of 40 test images were taken and segregated into groups, with 20 samples allocated to each method. Implementation was conducted using Python, and statistical analysis was performed using Clincalc.com. The study set a statistical power of 85%, with alpha level of 0.05 and 0.2 beta level set to ensure a thorough analysis. Performance was assessed based on accuracy, with R-CNN achieving 96.461%, significantly outperforming CNN, which recorded an accuracy of 83.583%. The statistical comparison yielded a two-tailed significance value of p < 0.001, highlighting the superior efficiency of R-CNN in text extraction tasks. These findings underscore the potential of R-CNN as a preferred approach for achieving higher accuracy in text extraction applications.

articleTitle: Integrating Machine Learning and Deep Learning for Accurate Fraud Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Credit card fraud detection is a major challenge for the financial industry, and its prevention requires machine learning models to be accurate and efficient in reducing financial losses. This paper proposes a comparative analysis of three most popular machine learning models DT, RF, and XGB that can be applied for fraud detection. To optimize the model’s performance, we apply RFE to select only the most important features for the classification process. Each of the models has been evaluated for their performance through several metrics including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC, to validate its effectiveness on detecting fraudulent transactions. We have also analyzed each model’s computational efficiency, not only in training but also for inference time because the real-time nature of this task is so crucial. While our results have shown that XGB outperformed DT and RF in both accuracy and AUC-ROC, it really does need fine hyperparameter tuning to optimize its computational cost. The results of the paper provide excellent insights for banks that want to deploy machine learning models for detecting fraud, by offering a compromise between model performance and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Speech Recognition and Transcription
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel speech-to-text model. This is a user-friendly platform designed to convert spoken text into written text efficiently and accurately. It allows users to record their speech, transcribe in real time and saves output in a downloadable format such as pdf. It offers features such as language selection and real-time display of transcribed text. By supporting multiple languages such as (English, Hindi, Marathi, Tamil, Bengali), it addresses the needs of a global audience. Overall, this offers a versatile and accessible solution for converting speech to text, making it a valuable tool for users across different fields. This paper details the system’s architecture, methodologies employed, and the results of extensive testing across different languages and audio qualities. The system’s impact on accessibility and productivity in multilingual environments is discussed, with potential areas for future enhancement outlined.

articleTitle: Deep Learning approach for Identification and Classification of Tulsi Leaf Disease
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Tulsi (Ocimum sanctum) is commonly known as holy basil; it consists of numerous amounts of medicinal value. It is popular not only for the medicinal value it has, but also for its spiritual significance in many parts of the world for its healing and traditional aspects. However, environmental destruction and not taking care of the Tulsi plant can impact the leaves and overall growth of the plant. This approach helps improve Tulsi plant health by using a smart application. The dataset used is collected from the local environments from different locality to get different insights on the Tulsi plant. The dataset is then preprocessed to enhance the data quality and model performance. This application incorporates features which is user friendly interface and allows individuals to check on the plant with very effortless way and in addition to this it helps user to detect the diseased leaves prior rather than last. This model not only helps the individuals but also contributes in conservation of Tulsi by promoting a healthy growth of the plant.
