By proper identification of the healthy and unhealthy leaves this application promotes the proper measures to be maintained for the plant health which ensures a very strong and healthy growth of the plant. This approach not only distinguishes the disease but also helps to conserve the Tulsi for the sustainability of earth as it also has the property of improving the air quality which is very essential for the environment.

articleTitle: Assistive Study on Paediatric Pulmonology With Respiratory Sounds
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The mortality rate due to respiratory diseases is around 44.0 per 100,000 of the paediatric population in recent years and ranks as the 6th cause of death worldwide. Lung auscultation is a cost-effective, non-invasive diagnostic tool in paediatric population where imaging tests are challenging. A public paediatric dataset containing 1,949 respiratory sounds comprised of four classes namely, continuous adventitious sounds (CAS), discontinuous adventitious sounds (DAS), combination, and normal has been used. The Bark Frequency Cepstral Coefficients have been extracted, employing Bark scale filters and discrete cosine transform to de-correlate them. These coefficients are able to perceive frequency resolution similar to human hearing system with better resilience to irrelevant noise components. These are then fed to a less complex model, Extreme Learning Machine algorithm to classify different respiratory sounds. This was tuned by defining the number of hidden neurons, activation functions, and other hyperparameters. The trained model provided the best accuracy of 98.19% with sigmoid activation function and 25 neurons for four classes. The proposed framework was able to achieve a precision of 100%, 95%, 99% and 100% for CAS, DAS, CAS & DAS and normal class. The proposed model assists the pulmonologists in articulating the symptoms in paediatric population.

articleTitle: The study on the impact of activation function and pooling strategies on U-Net-based medical image fusion of traumatic brain images
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Image fusion is the technique in which two or more images are merged to enrich the information content of the image. In this study fusion of CT and MRI images is carried out using U-net architecture-based CNN model. In CNN, activation function and pooling strategies play a main role in determining the quality enrichment of fused images. Activation functions (AF) provide non-linear learning, helping build robust training models with a wide range of feature extraction improving the model performance. Pooling is a technique used in CNN to down-sample the image and to improve the spatial dimension by retaining the information in the image. In this study, we aim to identify the combinations of activation function and pooling strategy to improve the neural network performance, we inspect the effectiveness of the ReLU and Sigmoid functions with a combination of max pooling and average pooling techniques. These combinations are evaluated using a series of metrics: Peak Signal Noise Ratio (PSNR), Structure Similarity Index (SSIM), Mean Squared Error (MSE), Entropy, Fusion Factor, Mutual Information (MI), and Edge Preservation with the best values of 70.0073, 0.8547, 15.61, 1.2205, 0.8546, 0.2559, 0.3388 respectively. The results imply that the ReLU activation function, when united with max pooling, consistently improves the performance of the U-Net model in most measures. This combination provides better performance extraction and preserves important details in the processed image.

articleTitle: Optimized U-Net Model for Advanced Road Extraction Using Satellite Images
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Extracting accurate road networks from high-resolution satellite images is the key feature for updating geospatial databases and supporting autonomous navigation. However automatic road extraction is a difficult task due to various aspects like shadows, occlusion of buildings, trees, and varying road conditions that hinder precise extraction. This paper focuses on using the hybrid loss function that integrates dice loss, binary crossentropy, and focal loss that enable the optimized U-Net architecture to counter the class imbalance and mitigate the impact of small road segments. The experiment is conducted on a DeepGlobe dataset that demonstrates improved performance metrics and road connectivity compared to state-of-the-art methods. Overall, our model enhances the ability to extract the road network accurately.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study of Solid Waste Classification using Deep Learning and Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Solid Waste Management (SWM) involves the strategic planning and procedural management of solid wastes, which is a key factor in sustainable development of municipalities from physical, logical, and legal-political perspectives. Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) is typically managed using four methods: composting, recycling, landfilling, and incineration for reuse. The absence of proper on-site solid waste treatment increases the burden on urban municipalities, as the growing volume of waste demands methods such as recycling and source separation, along with classification for disposal. In mining activities, large volumes of Mining-Associated Solid wastes (MASW) are generated across various stages including exploration, separation, concentration, crushing, and sorting. Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) techniques have been employed in solid waste classification to categorize wastes as organic and recyclable. The conventional ML and DL techniques include Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Graph Long Short-Term Memory (GLSTM) employed for solid waste classification. The performance metrics of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score are used to evaluate the models’ effectiveness of ML and DL techniques in solid waste classification.

articleTitle: Sentiment Analysis-Based Product Review System for Enhanced Recommendations
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce has resulted in an overwhelming amount of user-generated content in the form of product reviews. Harnessing these reviews effectively is critical for enhancing recommendation systems. This paper presents a sentiment analysis-based approach that delves into specific product attributes, such as quality, design, price, durability, usability, comfort, value for money, and customer service, to extract actionable insights. By employing natural language processing (NLP) techniques, our system calculates both overall and attribute-specific sentiment scores, which are aggregated into a comprehensive recommendation score. The proposed methodology bridges the gap between unstructured text reviews and structured product recommendations, offering a detailed, attribute-focused perspective to improve user decision-making.

articleTitle: Predicting Tesla Stock Prices Using AI Techniques: An Analysis of Historical Trends, Trading Volumes, and Market Volatility
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Predicting stock market trends, especially for highly volatile stocks such as Tesla, presents unique challenges and opportunities. This study leverages deep learning, machine learning (ML), and time-series analysis as artificial intelligence (AI) tools to forecast Tesla's stock prices. The research aims to create robust predictive models by analyzing historical data, trading volumes, and market volatility [3][16]. The findings provide actionable insights for investors and uncover factors influencing Tesla stock performance. Models such as Long-Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Auto Regressive Integrated Moving Average(ARIMA), Gradient Boosting, and Random Forest are evaluated for prediction precision [1] [17], with SHapley Additive exPlanations(SHAP) employed for feature impact analysis.

articleTitle: Detecting and Mitigating Bias in LLMs through Knowledge Graph-Augmented Training
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Large language models have revolutionized natural language processing with their surprising capability to understand and generate human-like text. However, many of these models inherit and further amplify the biases present in their training data, raising ethical and fairness concerns. The detection and mitigation of such biases are vital to ensuring that LLMs act responsibly and equitably across diverse domains. This work investigates Knowledge Graph-Augmented Training (KGAT) as a novel method to mitigate bias in LLM. Using structured domain-specific knowledge from real-world knowledge graphs, we improve the understanding of the model and reduce biased output. Public datasets for bias assessment include Gender Shades, Bias in Bios, and FairFace, while metrics such as demographic parity and equal opportunity facilitate rigorous detection. We also performed targeted mitigation strategies to correct biased associations, leading to a significant drop in biased output and improved bias metrics. Equipped with real-world datasets and knowledge graphs, our framework is both scalable and effective, paving the way toward responsible deployment in sensitive and high-stakes applications.

articleTitle: Ethical Frameworks for Artificial Intelligence: A Comparative Study
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The fast-paced evolution of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has given rise to critical ethical challenges leading to various frameworks proposed by government and industry leaders regarding the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence. This report compares AI ethics policies, from the European Union (EU), the United States (US), Canada and Asia, as well as the efforts of major AI companies. Whereas the EU has a regulatory-centric model with a focus on stringent oversight, the US has a more malleable, innovation-driven one. In Canada, such a direct approach on behalf of the government is missing — with an emphasis on transparency and accountability, several government directives deal with the issue of the impact on COVID-19 and on the relevant parties involved. Within, big firms of AI, such as Google, Microsoft, and IBM, have developed guidelines that spotlight fairness, transparency, accountability, and the quality of knowledge. The paper also investigates the cost of these ethics frameworks, and their adoption rates. The study investigates the different approaches and highlights international differences in the balance between innovation and ethics through a comparison of these strategies. Moreover, since quality data is essential for AI, maintaining high data quality is mentioned as one of the key factors of AI ethics standardization. With AI's insights penetrating many sectors and industries, the demand for well-planned ethics policies is more crucial than ever in determining how AI will evolve according to societal goals and mitigate risks. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Classification of Hydroponic Lettuce Leaves using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Hydroponic lettuce, known for its rich nutritional content and medicinal properties, holds immense potential as a staple vegetable. However, the emergence of yellow and rotten leaves due to nutrient deficiencies poses significant challenges in maintaining quality and efficiency during production. Manual sorting of these abnormal leaves before packing incurs high labor costs and inefficiencies, necessitating the development of automated sorting systems. Further, it is easy to classify the good leaves among the available stock. In this work, the four classes being considered are Fully Nutritious, Nitrogen, Potassium and Phosphorous Deficient leaves. Texture features help in identifying the physical condition and health of the leaves, capturing details related to the leaf surface which can indicate nutrient deficiencies. Color features, on the other hand, are crucial for detecting changes in leaf pigmentation, which often signal specific nutrient deficiencies. KNN, SVM, and CNN are used in this work. KNN relies on nearby data points for classification, while SVM constructs optimal decision boundaries in high-dimensional spaces. CNN leverages convolutional layers for deep feature extraction from image data. The performance of all the methods is assessed using confusion matrix. Experimental results specify that the proposed method gives better accuracy for four classes.

articleTitle: AI-Based Image Classification for Indian Temple Iconography: A CNN-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: India is a country that encompasses a vast and diverse cultural and historical legacy, including numerous architecturally significant sculptures in temples. Analyzing and identifying entities in temple sculptures is a highly challenging and complex task. Digital archives with images, videos, books, interviews, and other resources can significantly accelerate iconographic research by building on past studies. This study explores image classification techniques applied to archives to enhance iconographic study. The findings contribute to the broader discourse on Indian art and culture, providing valuable insights into the intricate iconographic representations found in temple architecture.

articleTitle: Navigating Anomaly Detection in Complex Networks: Methods, Challenges, and Recent Advances
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The paper provides a comprehensive examination of the strategies and challenges in identifying anomalies within complex networks, which are crucial for maintaining the security and reliability of systems like social media, telecommunications, and financial networks. It classifies anomalies into different types—node, edge, subgraph, and temporal—each requiring specific detection methods. The paper reviews a broad spectrum of anomaly detection techniques, from traditional statistical methods to advanced machine learning and graph-based approaches. Recent advancements, particularly in deep learning with Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and autoencoders, have significantly enhanced the ability to detect anomalies in dynamic and high-dimensional networks. Privacy-preserving approaches like federated learning are also discussed, highlighting the growing need to secure data while maintaining detection efficiency. Challenges such as scalability, the evolving nature of networks, high-dimensional data, and the interpretability of detection models are critically analyzed. The paper advocates for future research focused on developing more adaptive, interpretable, and benchmarked models to handle the complexities of modern networks. Practical applications are demonstrated through case studies, emphasizing the vital role of anomaly detection in real-world network management.

articleTitle: Cricket Player’s Performance Prediction Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This paper presents a predictive model for cricket player performance utilizing machine learning techniques to optimize team selection for competitive matches. By analyzing historical performance data, opponent dynamics, and stadium conditions, the model aims to identify the most suitable combination of players—comprising 6 batsmen, 3 bowlers, and 2 all-rounders. Key inputs, including pitch type, batting and bowling preferences, and winning probabilities, are integrated into a rule-based algorithm. Data is collected through web scraping from reputable sources such as ESPN Cricinfo, facilitating accurate predictions based on batting and bowling averages. The findings highlight the effectiveness of combining traditional cricketing knowledge with advanced data analytics to enhance decision-making in team management.

articleTitle: FraudGuard: Advancing Credit Card Fraud Detection with Machine Learning Benchmarks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This research presents a comprehensive approach to credit card fraud detection, combining machine learning algorithms with user-centric applications. Analysing trends and fraudulent activities across various parameters, the study enhances fraud prevention strategies for stakeholders. Employing algorithms like XGBoost, Decision Tree, and Random Forest, and using SMOTE to balance the dataset, XGBoost achieved the highest accuracy. Practical tools developed include a real-time fraud detection app using Streamlit and a Tkinter-based desktop GUI, both leveraging the trained XGBoost model for instant predictions.

articleTitle: Forecasting the Prediction for Atmosphere Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This study includes machine learning techniques that are applied to historical meteorological data to propose an enhanced method of weather prediction. We systematically assess the performance of four algorithms: Decision Tree, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine and Logistic Regression, using a dataset that includes important meteorological variables. According to our experimental findings, the Random Forest algorithm attains the greatest accuracy at 88%, with Decision Tree model coming in second at 85%. While Logistic Regression exhibits a lower accuracy of 71%, the SVM model exhibits a noteworthy 76% accuracy. In order to increase predicted accuracy, this study emphasizes the importance of efficient feature selection, data preprocessing, and model optimization. We then go over how these discoveries may be used practically in various fields, like environmental observation, agriculture and disaster relief. The study highlights the potential for improving accuracy and dependability in actual weather prediction systems while offering useful details regarding the benefits and drawbacks of different machine learning approaches for atmospheric prediction.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning And Deep Learning Models For Predicting Stock Market Close Prices
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Stock price prediction is inherently challenging due to the volatile and nonlinear nature of financial markets. Traditional financial models often fail to capture these complexities, but advancements in machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) offer promising solutions. This study evaluates the performance of ML models (KNN, Linear Regression, Random Forest) and DL models (ANN, RNN, LSTM) in predicting stock closing prices using daily Open, High, and Low prices as inputs. The analysis focuses on American Airlines (AAL) and Delta Airlines (DAL) datasets, representing low and high volatility, respectively. Model performance is assessed using MSE, MAE, and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> metrics. Results demonstrate that DL models, particularly LSTMs, outperform traditional ML models and exhibit strong adaptability across volatility levels.

articleTitle: ECOSAUR - Empowering Sustainable Choices: A Mobile Application for Carbon Footprint Awareness and Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Climate change poses a critical global challenge, requiring urgent action to mitigate its impacts. One of the most effective ways to address this issue is by empowering individuals to make sustainable lifestyle choices. This paper examines the potential of mobile applications in reducing individual carbon footprints by providing users with data-driven insights and actionable strategies. The proposed carbon footprint tracking app consists of four main sections: a home overview page, a carbon footprint calculator, a dashboard for tracking greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, and a chatbot for interactive assistance. By collecting data on transportation, energy use, dietary choices, and domestic waste, the app calculates individual carbon footprints using established emission factors. This information allows users to make informed decisions to reduce their environmental impact. The paper highlights the significance of providing clear and accurate information to users, helping bridge the gap between awareness and actionable change. This mobile-based solution not only tracks carbon emissions but also motivates users to adopt sustainable practices, fostering a community-driven approach to carbon neutrality and climate action.

articleTitle: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Heart Disease: Comparing Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Bayesian Network Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Heart disease is still a global health challenge; thus, the model at an early stage of prediction in a timely intervention remains a challenge. It compares various techniques in machine learning, deep learning, and Bayesian networks against the UCI Cleveland Heart Disease dataset, whereby it compares with the Kaggle Heart Disease dataset. Attempts have been made for the following models: XGBoost, Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting, Logistic Regression (LR), Support Vector Classifier (SVM), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Bayesian Networks. One-hot encoding, ANOVA F-test-based feature selection, and SMOTE will be used for advanced preprocessing for higher performance. In ensemble methods, XGBoost was the best method with accuracy of about 97.32% while the second highest accuracy rate was given by Random Forest with about 95.89%. This result probably justifies the applicability of ensemble models in medical decisions. A very high performance was observed while using a measure that is derived from precision, recall, and F1-score. The paper puts into the limelight the necessity for feature engineering, missing data correction, and class imbalance correction for higher predictive reliability. Future research should be placed on DL with a more deep architecture and multiple data sets for the practical application in healthcare with improved prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: A Multimodal Method for Detecting Language through Speech in Ten Indian Languages
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This research presents the development of an audio-driven language prediction system aimed at recognizing and classifying Indian languages. The Random Forest machine learning model is employed by the system. It is developed using a unique dataset that includes audio samples from ten Indian languages: Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Punjabi, Tamil, Telugu, and Urdu. To improve the accuracy of language identification, the audio data is subjected to preprocessing steps, such as segmentation and noise reduction. Key audio features, including Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs), zero-crossing rate, spectral centroid, and chroma attributes, are obtained to represent the acoustic qualities of the languages. These features are then utilized to train the Random Forest classifier, which shows excellent effectiveness in distinguishing between the different languages. The suggested system was evaluated through accuracy metrics, demonstrating significant capability in correctly categorizing audio inputs according to their respective languages. This study tackles the challenges of multilingual speech recognition in a linguistically diverse country such as India and offers a scalable method for automatic language identification.

articleTitle: Leveraging MobileNet V2 for swift and precise identification of lung and colon cancers
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Lung and colon cancers pose a significant global health challenge. Early detection is crucial for improved patient outcomes. This study investigates Applying deep learning to differentiate lung and colon cancer subtypes using the LC25000 dataset. The MobileNetV2 architecture was selected due to its efficiency and accuracy. The dataset was divided into five categories: Colon adenocarcinoma, non-neoplastic colon tissue, Malignant lung adenocarcinoma, Malignant lung squamous cell carcinoma, and non-neoplastic lung tissue. Data augmentation techniques were applied to enhance model performance. The model achieved impressive accuracies of 97.57%, 98.00%, and 98.3% on the training, validation, and testing sets, respectively. These results highlight the potential of deep learning for rapid, accurate, and minimally invasive cancer detection, surpassing traditional methods. Our findings contribute to the development of more efficient and accessible cancer screening approaches.

articleTitle: Current Approaches in Abstractive Text Summarization: A Comprehensive Survey and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Abstractive text summarization is a complex task in natural language processing aimed at generating concise and coherent summaries that convey the essential meaning of documents. Research has shifted from extractive summarization to abstractive summarization which has new, condensed representations instead of simply extracting and rearranging existing sentences. Using encoder-decoder architecture, where the encoder processes the input text to generate a contextual representation, and the decoder produces the summary based on this representation. This paper provides a review of papers in the field of abstractive summarization from 2018 to 2024. The paper defines a methodology for in-depth analysis of recent research trends, datasets, preprocessing methods, feature selection, methods, evaluation metrics, and challenges with text summarization. The models like BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) and GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer) have propelled the field forward.Abstractive summarization finds applications in numerous fields, including news, academic research, legal documents, and social media, enhancing information retrieval and natural language understanding. This paper aims to help researchers know about abstractive summarization methods that are interpretable, robust, and adaptable across various languages and domains.

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Detection of Anemia Using Deep Learning on Conjunctival Images
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Anemia, characterized by low levels of red blood cells or hemoglobin, affects millions worldwide, significantly affecting public health. Traditional diagnostic methods, while effective, are invasive, costly, and inaccessible in resource-constrained settings. This paper proposes a non-invasive approach for anemia detection using conjunctival images analyzed through deep learning techniques. The proposed methodology involves capturing high-resolution conjunctival images, pre-processing them, and using a customized Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for feature extraction and classification. The results achieved by the customized CNN fine-tuned with a batch size of 16 give an Accuracy of 96%, Precision of 95%, Recall of 96%, and ROC-AUC score of 0.99. The customized CNN outperformed the other models for this work, such as Random Forest, XGBoost, SVM, ResNet50, and MobileNetV2. This work highlights the potential for non-invasive diagnostic tools to improve accessibility and efficiency in healthcare, particularly for underserved populations. The findings endorse integrating deep learning in healthcare as a transformative approach to address global challenges such as anemia.

articleTitle: Supply chain tracking of drugs using Ethereum
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Counterfeiting, increased fake intermediate products, lack of transparency, unauthorized alteration of data, and other related problems throughout the supply chain have made it necessary for the modern pharmaceutical industry to ensure integrity and security. Thus, the above-mentioned problem can be solved by a decentralized blockchain-based system, which ensures security and traceability. In the proposed solution, there are seven stakeholders including manufacturers and consumers. Authorized manufacturers are allowed to store the drugs in the blockchain network, and corresponding QR and bar codes are generated. This generates a reliable record of drug movements by constructing an architecture that is decentralized to avoid alteration of the data by anyone. Consumers have the opportunity to scan QR codes to ensure that their products are genuine and trace their origin. By addressing the challenges of the conventional pharmaceutical supply chain that provides high transparency, minimal counterfeits, and assured data security, this system addresses the aforementioned disadvantages.

articleTitle: Hybrid Deep Neural Network for Classification of Malaria Parasites in Microscopic Images
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Malaria is a critical epidemic disease transmitted by bites from female Anopheles mosquitoes, caused by Plasmodium parasites. Although it does not spread directly between people, early detection is essential to prevent mild cases from progressing. This research develops a hybrid deep-learning model for classifying malaria parasites in thin blood smears including infected and uninfected erythrocytes. The model employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) with recurrent neural network (RNN) variants. To advance interpretability, the Explainable AI technique, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Map (GradCAM), is incorporated to highlight key regions in the image that support the model's decision-making. Additionally, regularization techniques, including data augmentation, batch normalization, and L2 regularization, are applied to enhance model performance. The proposed CNN-BiGRU model achieved a validation accuracy of 96.7%, precision of 0.97%, recall of 0.96%, F1-score of 0.97%, and an AUC of 0.99 on both training and testing sets.

articleTitle: Sustainable Urban Waste Management: A Scalable IoT System for Automated Segregation and Real-Time Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Rapid urban population growth has exacerbated waste management challenges, leading to overflowing bins and public health risks. This paper presents an innovative IoT-enabled waste segregation and monitoring system designed to improve urban sanitation and sustainability. Equipped with ultrasonic, infrared, and moisture sensors, the system autonomously categorizes waste and tracks bin fill levels. Data collected is transmitted through a wireless mesh network to a central server, enabling real-time monitoring and data-driven waste disposal decisions. When bin levels exceed 70%, alerts are sent to municipal authorities via GSM for timely collection. The system is powered by an Arduino UNO microcontroller, which manages sensor operations and data flow, significantly enhancing waste management efficiency. By facilitating automated waste segregation and providing actionable insights, this system supports the development of cleaner, smarter cities and aligns with global sustainability initiatives, promoting urban cleanliness, resource efficiency, and environmental stewardship.

articleTitle: Enhancing Human Safety through Modesty Guard: A Comprehensive Review of OpenCV-Based Surveillance Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The increasing deployment of reconnaissance organizations in civic and isolated places has raised concerns about privacy, ethics, and cultural sensitivities, particularly when it comes to the unintended capture of nudity or other immodest imagery. In diverse environments where cultural norms dictate specific standards of modesty, there is a growing need for systems that can automatically detect and manage nudity in surveillance footage without infringing on individuals' rights or exposing sensitive material unnecessarily. This system utilizes artificial intelligence (AI) and computer vision to detect nudity in real-time video feeds, offering customizable responses such as blurring, alerting security personnel, or securely archiving sensitive footage. This paper outlines the technical architecture, deployment strategies, and deep learning algorithms of the Modesty Guard system, emphasizing its potential applications in various environments where surveillance and modesty concerns intersect. Through the use of advanced AI and real-time video processing, the system promotes ethical surveillance practices while respecting cultural diversity and privacy.

articleTitle: SmartFood AI: A Multimodal Framework for Accessible Nutritional Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This work presents an advanced food detection system leveraging computer vision and AI to enhance food recognition and nutritional analysis, aligning with global health goals set by organizations like World Health Organization (WHO) and the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO). These organizations emphasize the critical role of nutrition in public health and advocate for accessible, accurate dietary information to combat malnutrition and promote balanced diets. Powered by a deep learning based framework, the proposed system delivers high-precision food identification through a bounding box regressor for localization and a knowledge graph for nutritional insights. Its zero-shot learning capability enables recognition of previously unseen foods without additional training, addressing the limitations of traditional systems by providing accurate identification alongside contextual nutritional data. This adaptability allows the system to evolve with changing dietary trends and meet diverse user needs, supporting applications in healthcare, personal nutrition monitoring, and food. Moreover; It is beneficial for visually impaired individuals, enhancing autonomy by enabling them to recognize foods and access essential nutritional information independently, thereby promoting healthier living. The system demonstrates robust performance across varied conditions, making it effective for both personal use and public health applications. By providing critical dietary insights and adapting to new foods, this AI-powered solution represents a scalable and impactful tool in computer vision and dietary monitoring.It promotes global health initiatives and personal well-being by providing a useful strategy for raising awareness of nutrition and encouraging better lifestyles.

articleTitle: Bridging the Diagnostic Gap: Classification of MRI-Based Brain Tumors Using a CNN and Transformer-Based Hybrid Deep Learning Method
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Accurate classification of brain tumors in Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans is pivotal for timely clinical intervention, yet remains challenging due to intricate anatomical variations and overlapping imaging features. This research addresses this gap by proposing a hybrid deep learning architecture that synergizes 2D Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), 3D CNNs, and Transformer-Based attention mechanisms. The framework leverages pre-trained 2D CNN models—MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetV2B0—to extract spatial hierarchies from axial MRI slices, while a 3D CNN captures volumetric dependencies inherent in multi-dimensional MRI data. A Transformer block, equipped with multi-head self-attention, further refines feature representation by modeling long-range contextual relationships across image regions. The model is trained on a publicly available MRI dataset comprising four tumor classes (glioma, meningioma, pituitary, and non-tumorous), with preprocessing steps including intensity normalization, resizing, and augmentation (rotation, flipping, shear) to bolster generalization. Training optimization integrates ReduceLROnPlateau (learning rate reduction upon stagnated validation loss) and EarlyStopping (halting training at performance plateau) strategies to ensure efficient convergence. The hybrid architecture demonstrates robust diagnostic capability, achieving state-of-the-art classification performance, thereby underscoring its potential as an automated, reliable tool for multi-class brain tumor identification in clinical oncology workflows.

articleTitle: Context is King: Rethinking Query Expansion in Modern Search Engines
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: In the era of digital information overload, search engines have evolved beyond simple keyword matching to embrace context-aware methodologies. However, the task of accurately interpreting user intent remains a critical challenge, with traditional query expansion techniques often falling short of capturing semantic and contextual nuances. This paper critically examines the evolution of query expansion strategies, highlighting their limitations and exploring state-of-the-art techniques such as machine learning models, knowledge graphs, and transformer-based systems like BERT and GPT. Experimental results compare traditional methods like synonym expansion with modern approaches, demonstrating the superior relevance and diversity of results from context-aware systems. The study underscores the importance of integrating real-time contextual signals and dynamic user preferences to enhance search engine performance, paving the way for more personalized and accurate retrieval systems.

articleTitle: Dementia Prediction Using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)

authors.preferredName: Boggavarapu V B S Pavan Kumar

abstract: Dementia is one of the progressive neurological disorders. The challenge is significantly high in terms of benefits to patients and health systems globally. Hence, an earlier and accurate prediction regarding the occurrence of dementia leads to timely intervention and better outcomes. In this regard, this paper presents a novel method of predicting dementia onset using deep learning techniques combined with Bayesian networks. Our results show that the proposed model outperforms traditional predictive methods, suggesting that this deep learning-Bayesian framework could serve as a valuable tool for early dementia diagnosis.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Traditional Machine Learning, Deep Neural Network, and Statistical Modeling for Music Genre Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: A range of general features of music, such as Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients and spectrograms, is used to describe musically descriptive confines of different genres. While such a comparison is made between traditional machine learning models, like SVMs and random forests, with the more elaborative work on deep-learning architectures like CNNs, RNNs, and probabilistic techniques like Bayesian networks, which capture uncertainty and perhaps provide a more fine-grained prediction. Deep-learning models, especially CNNs, appear to achieve high accuracies in music genre classification over the GTZAN dataset. Probabilistic models, however, have the advantage of handling noisy or incomplete data by enforcing some meaningful interpretation of the underlying relations between features and genres. This research provides a thorough comparison of these techniques and aids in improving the music genre classification systems.

articleTitle: Bridging the Emotional Gap in AI: A Study on Speech Emotion Recognition for Adaptive Human Computer Interaction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)

authors.preferredName: V S S L Deepak Janapa

abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) is an advancement that has attracted a lot of interest because of its potential uses in intelligent systems, mental health monitoring, and human-computer interaction (HCI). Even with the progress made in AI-driven HCI, many systems are still unable to accurately sense and comprehend human emotions. Virtual assistants may carry out tasks based on spoken instructions, but they don't react well to user’s emotions, which results in less-than-ideal interactions. In order to close this gap, this study implements a speech emotion recognition algorithm that uses the Ryerson Audio-Visual Database of Emotional Speech and Song (RAVDESS), and Toronto Emotional Speech Set (TESS) datasets to examine voice characteristics. The system makes use of cutting-edge deep learning methods including Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to capture temporal relationships in speech patterns and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for feature extraction from spectrograms which results in building a Hybrid Model. Traditional machine learning models may not be able to capture subtle emotional nuances in complex data, but they do offer faster processing times and easier implementations. Conversely, deep learning models, including 2D architecture such as CNNs and LSTMs, need more processing power but are better at handling large datasets and detecting subtle emotional cues. By leveraging these advancements, this research aims to enhance virtual assistants and similar systems to better recognize and respond to emotional cues in real time. Thus, Opening the door for a technological environment that is more user-centered and sympathetic.

articleTitle: Guided View Approach for Lane Detection and Caution Analysis using Computer Vision and Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: In recent years, advancements in computer vision technology have enabled innovative applications in various fields, including transportation safety. One such application is a Lane Detection and Caution Measurement Analyzer system aimed at enhancing road safety. This system uses computer vision techniques to provide real-time analysis of road conditions, helping drivers navigate more safely. The Lane Detection module employs image processing algorithms such as edge detection, Hough transform, and perspective transformation to identify lane boundaries accurately. Additionally, the Caution Measurement Analyzer module utilizes object detection and tracking algorithms to identify potential hazards, such as potholes, and measures the caution required for safe driving. The proposed model integrates CNN, OpenCV, and YOLO, achieving 87% accuracy in object detection and caution measurement, and 94% accuracy in lane boundary detection.

articleTitle: Real-Time Gender Classification from Facial Images Using VGG16 and GoogLeNet Architectures
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Facial attribute recognition, particularly gender classification, has gained unprecedented interest in various fields like security, personalized marketing, and human-computer interaction in recent years. In this research, we dive into the deep learning realm and use transfer learning-based models for real-time gender classification from facial images. We use both VGG16 (Visual Geometry Group 16-layer network) and GoogLeNet structures as our feature extraction backbone, with pre-trained weights on ImageNet to exploit the tremendous results obtained on relatively small and targeted datasets. Robust real-world variability is made through heavy use of data augmentation techniques such as rotation, scaling, and flipping. The preprocessed dataset feeds into the models whose optimized hyperparameters incur both accuracy and efficiency. Experimental results show that although the VGG16 and GoogLeNet models offer high accuracy and adaptability for gender classification tasks, each of their architectures possesses a different strength in processing speed and feature representation. The paper gives insights on the comparative performance of these architectures in the context of gender classification with potential applications in a myriad number of fields that require rapid and reliable demographic profiling.

articleTitle: Enhanced Sentiment Analysis of Twitter(X) Data Using an Ensemble Stacking Model
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Analysis of user sentiment and behavior on social media platforms, especially on Twitter (X), is becoming increasingly important now. This paper proposes a Stacking Classifier as an Ensemble Machine Learning Algorithm for improving the sentiment analysis on Twitter (X). Here, Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, and SVM are taken as base classifiers and Logistic Regression (LR) is taken as a meta-learner for combining the outcome of all learners. The study uses the Tf-Idf approach in processing textual data to efficiently quantify and categorize text for sentiment analysis. text for sentiment analysis. Results from the proposed model are evaluated by employing ROC-AUC, F1-Score, Accuracy, Precision, and Recall metrics to guarantee performance efficacy. Nearly 89.70% accuracy was achieved by the layered classifier. We examined and performed comprehensive experiments with two important referenced works: the SVM, Random Forest (RF) and Decision Tree (DT) algorithm technique by Jyotsna Singh and Pradeep Tripathi [1] and the Ensemble Machine Learning technique by Pavlo Radiuk, Olga Pavlova, and Nadiia Hrypynska [2]. The model's ROC-AUC Score indicates its efficacy to distinguish between positive and negative data, and its continually strong performance demonstrates its dependability. The polarity score of 0.95 highlights the stark difference between the text's positive and negative emotions, indicating a very favorable mood. This research is noteworthy for its creation and implementation of a dependable approach for combining numerous classifiers using Meta-Learning. This method leads to higher accuracy and a more resilient sentiment analysis model. The results suggest that the Stacking Classifier is a useful technique for analyzing social network sentiment in more detail, which helps to understand the population's views and decisions

articleTitle: Enhanced Brain Stroke Prediction: A Bayesian Network-Integrated Ensemble Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Stroke remains a predominant global health issue, underscoring the critical necessity of sophisticated predictive models that can elevate diagnostic accuracy and optimize therapeutic interventions. In this study, we propose an advanced stroke prediction framework that leverages an ensemble of Logistic Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Bayesian Network classifiers, meticulously integrated to improve predictive performance. Among the classifiers, the Bayesian Network model achieved a remarkable accuracy of 99.78% on the "brain_stroke" dataset, demonstrating superior performance over the other ensemble models and highlighting the efficacy of probabilistic graphical models in stroke prediction. The proposed methodology offers a robust, high- accuracy diagnostic tool, facilitating early stroke detection, timely clinical intervention, and enhanced resource allocation, thereby contributing significantly to improved patient outcomes and healthcare efficiency.

articleTitle: The BUNK - An advanced voice assistant interface with Natural Language Processing and Artificial Intelligence using Python
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: In the world of digital innovation, voice assistants play an important role as bridges between human-technology interaction. The goal of this research is to use natural language processing (NLP) and artificial intelligence (AI) to create a sophisticated voice assistant application using Python. Through a detailed analysis of natural language processing (NLP) techniques and artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms, the proposed application seeks to overcome conventional constraints and enable continuous user-digital environment interaction. By facilitating seamless navigation across a broad range of tasks, the voice assistant’s extensive capabilities and emphasis on user-friendly aesthetics have the potential to completely transform how people interact with technology. Considering Python’s growing importance in contemporary software development, this study emphasizes Python’s adaptability and suggests a fundamental change in the way humans and computers interact.

articleTitle: Apparel Recommendation System using Rule based Filtering and SMOTE for Online Shopping
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The Apparel Recommendation System (ARS) is a machine learning-based platform designed to enhance the shopping experience by providing personalized apparel suggestions based on user preferences such as type, color, price range, and ratings. The user interface, developed with Tkinter, is simple and interactive, allowing effortless selections through drop-down menus and sliders. On the backend, SMOTE (Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique) addresses dataset imbalances, ensuring fair representation across apparel categories. A rule-based filtering approach aligns recommendations with user-selected preferences, resulting in accurate suggestions. Additionally, a live chat feature, integrated with React.js, Node.js, and Socket.io, offers real-time assistance. The curated dataset improves recommendation accuracy, enabling users to quickly find apparel that matches their individual styles.

articleTitle: Asamyuta Hasta Mudras Recognition Using MediaPipe Keypoint Extraction and Random Forest Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Bharatanatyam is a dance of Tamil Nadu in southern India. This dance form includes the hand gestures known as the Mudras which holds immense symbolic meaning and play a vital role in storytelling. Each mudra carries its own essence, depicting various emotions, deities, and natural elements. We are here focusing on the Asamyuta hasta mudras or single hand gestures are expressions to be shown by a hand. This work addresses mudra recognition by framing it as a 28-class classification problem. This is achieved by utilizing MediaPipe for hand key points in a CSV format and demonstrates effective performance even with a limited dataset. This will achieve robust mudras recognition through a supervised machine learning model.

articleTitle: Exploring Religions and Cross-Cultural Sensitivities in Conversational AI
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: With the fast growth of conversational AI, it is very important that these systems can handle religion and cultural sensitivity correctly. New, cutting-edge models like BERT, mBERT (multilingual BERT), and XLM-RoBERTa are very good at many types of natural language processing. But not a lot is known about how well they talk and act about their religious views. The dataset primarily contains content related to Christianity, Islam, and Hinduism, reflecting their prevalence in online discussions and AI training corpora. AIs need to learn how to deal with harsh words, social nuances, and touchy topics where they can talk about religion. Artificial intelligence systems could give answers that don't seem to be legit or different meaning which are very sensitive. This is a big ethical problem.We look at how well BERT, mBERT, and XLM-RoBERTa can handle religious and cultural situations in this study. We focus on how well they do across languages using the PAWS-X dataset. PAWS-X is a good tool for testing cross-lingual transfer because it has goals for finding paraphrases in a number of different languages. This lets us see how well these models understand complex meanings in a variety of linguistic and cultural settings. We use the dataset to test how well the model works in talks about Hinduism, Islam, and Christianity, which are very sensitive to cultural and religious differences.To see how well these models can understand underlying cultural differences and come up with suitable responses, we test them on religious sentence pairs as part of our methodology. We test both their language skills and their ability to stay sensitive when religious or doctrinal information is present. We also look into their cross-lingual transfer skills to see how well they work in different religious meaning. BERT, mBERT, and XLM-RoBERTa perform well in basic tasks but struggle with religious and cultural nuances. BERT and mBERT handle multiple languages effectively but often falter in unclear religious contexts, especially when switching between languages with unique religious terms.In this study, we assess sensitivity by analyzing model responses for their ability to correctly interpret religious connotations, avoid offensive language, and acknowledge cultural context. We apply sentiment analysis, contextual relevance scoring, and manual validation from domain experts to measure how well these models handle sensitive topics.

articleTitle: Mediguide:A Machine Learning based Smart Prescription System for Personalized Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This project uses a Decision Tree Classifier model which gives accurate health predictions based on the symptoms provided by users. The model has been trained at thousands of symptoms against diseases and thus predicts very accurately for the inputted data provided by the user. The system has an easy-to-use interface that helps users input their symptoms with ease and get instant predictions of potential diseases. In addition to predicting ailments, the application provides extensive information on the detected disease. Users are given a comprehensive breakdown of the disease, recommended medications, precautions, and personalized advice on diet and exercise regimes. It provides health insights that are meant to help users better manage their health and make better lifestyle decisions. With feedback loops, prediction accuracy and user experience can always be improved directly without worrying much about each setup. It seeks to use advanced technology to make practical health advice possible. Combining disease prediction in real time with meaningful health advice creates added value for users and encourages informed health choices. It enables users to own their health by providing them with a complete picture of their possible health problems and possible solutions to address them. This Project provides a powerful tool for more proactive users, with its combo of predictive analytics and health education resources.(And it helps us recognise the sport itself the user-friendly and detailed output that makes it easy and helpful for everyone to understand their health and what they can do about it.) It upskill traditionally trained AI learners to be perpendicular over ruinous health data towards an accessibly governed future, furnished with health facts and outcomes to improvement on the go.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Exploration of Acute Febrile Illnesses with Low Platelet Count Syndrome: From Epidemiology to AI-Driven Solutions
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This narrative review provides an in-depth examination of acute febrile illnesses with thrombocytopenia. Utilizing a robust and systematic literature search strategy, the study has identified and analyzed relevant studies to comprehensively understand these conditions. The review addresses the epidemiology of these syndromes, detailing their incidence, prevalence, and geographic distribution. The study explores a wide range of etiologies and the pathophysiological mechanisms that result in low platelet counts. Insights into the clinical presentation and diagnostic criteria are offered, highlighting the symptomatic spectrum and methods for accurate diagnosis. The discussion extends to management and treatment options specific to different etiologies, as well as potential complications and their prognostic implications. Preventive and control measures are also examined to emphasize the significance of public health interventions. Furthermore, the review investigates the promising role of artificial intelligence in the early prediction and diagnosis of these diseases, suggesting pathways for enhanced patient outcomes and more efficient healthcare strategies.

articleTitle: Bridging Intuition and Data: A Dynamic Framework for IPL Player Valuation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The Indian Premier League (IPL) is a professional Twenty20 cricket league. As part of the team formation for this league players are sold to teams through a competitive auction, often fetching high prices that may not reflect their performance—or surprisingly low ones despite their talent, for various factors. The auctions as of now, are conducted primarily based on intuition and on manual performance analysis. This paper proposes a comprehensive framework that transcends conventional performance indicators by integrating additional factors such as player fitness, availability, adaptability to different formats, social media influence, and global marketability. The objective is to address the lack of a robust player valuation model by systematically aligning team requirements with a player’s overall value. The proposed framework facilitates accurate monetary valuation of players both prior to and dynamically during the auction process, enhancing decision-making and fostering fairness in team formation.

articleTitle: Optimizing Arbitrage Opportunities in Automated Market Makers Using Scalable Blockchain Flash Loans
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This paper delves into the innovative application of flash loans within decentralized finance (DeFi), specifically in automated market maker (AMM) models. These systems streamline trading and improve liquidity through algorithmic asset pricing. However, high transaction fees and network congestion hinder their scalability. This research proposes strategies to optimize gas fees and enhance scalability by incorporating dynamic gas pricing and efficient fee management. By leveraging both Ethereum and Polygon networks, the system adapts to network conditions and addresses throughput limitations. The paper underscores the benefits of flash loans, including increased liquidity, cost efficiency, and risk mitigation, which are essential for arbitrage opportunities. Ultimately, this work aims to strengthen the DeFi ecosystem by promoting more robust and efficient trading strategies, paving the way for future innovations and greater financial inclusivity. Furthermore, a mathematical analysis of transactions, including profit and loss differences, is conducted to compare traditional arbitrage methods with the proposed scalable and efficient AMM-based approach.

articleTitle: Optimizing Travel Through AI: The Intersection of Data Quality and Customer Experience
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Artificial Intelligence is ever-evolving and so are its many applications in travel, covering anything from tailor-made trip suggestions to most innovative pricing tactics to conversational agents and predictive maintenance. This is because to build AI-based effective solutions, they are highly dependent on the quality of the data being used. Bad or insufficient data can result in regrettable consequences, wasted effort, and unhappy customers. This paper explores this essential link between the role of AI and data quality in enhancing travel experiences. It highlights that data management practices play a significant role in improving AI performance in travel. The paper covers targeted dimensions, including customer-facing, supply chain booking, and operational enhancement segments, while emphasizing the need for accurate and precise data for AI computational models. Through real-world case studies, this paper proves that companies emphasizing data quality often have an advantage in AI performance. The paper also elaborates on the key challenges pertaining to massive data processing, algorithmic biases, and data privacy laws. The paper closes with suggestions on how to use better data governance and data quality control to improve AI outcomes, thereby detailing a clear path for travel companies seeking to leverage AI technologies successfully. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Prediction of Household Energy Consumption: An LSTM Approach with High Precision
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Accurate forecasting of household electricity consumpation used for is crutial for demand management and smart grid operations. This study employs a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to predict electricity usage using four years of high-resolution energy data, including variables such as active and reactive power, voltage, and sub-metering values. preprocessing methods such as data smoothing, stationarity adjustments, and time-based feature extraction, was conducted to enhance model performance. The model demonstrated remarkable results with a training Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.0074, Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.0102, and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.9999, alongside a testing MAE of 0.0092, MSE of 0.0123, and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.9998. These results demonstrate the model’s ability to accurately capture complex consumption patterns and provide reliable forecasts for energy management applications

articleTitle: Enhancing Fare Prediction Accuracy in Ride Hailing Through Neural Networks and Data Simulation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Prediction of fare is the need for better service quality and effective pricing strategies that make for enhanced customer experiences in a ride-hailing service. From the identified features based on rides and ride-hailing activities - the distance covered, the time used for travel, number of passengers, and the main purposes of trips, the researchers will create a neural network model using such synthesized data to make real-time predictions for an accurate total fare estimate. This synthesis helps to understand the noise and natural variability in the ride-hailing datasets by showing different interaction patterns of the features over time. The analysis techniques used include scatter plots, correlation matrices, and time-series evaluations that reveal strong connections between fare amounts and distance traveled and trip duration. The dataset used in this research was sourced from Kaggle, ensuring a reliable foundation for training and evaluating the model. The proposed neural network architecture achieved 90% accuracy, with Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.5 units and Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 2.3 units, demonstrating its reliability. This paper shows how neural networks might be applicable to fare predictions and, therefore, can contribute toward artificial datasets with practical models applicable in the real world.

articleTitle: Enhancing Code Intelligence with CodeT5: A Unified Approach to Code Analysis and Generation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Recent advancements in deep learning have profoundly impacted various domains, including software development. This research primarily focuses on converting natural language descriptions into executable code—a transformative technique that converts natural language descriptions into executable code. Leveraging the T5 along with its specialized variant, CodeT5, this work aims to enhance developer productivity and code quality. To fine-tune these models, we utilize the MBPP (Mostly Basic Python Programming) benchmark dataset, ensuring their proficiency across diverse programming tasks. Traditional software development demands significant manual effort and technical expertise. Automating code generation from natural language inputs streamlines workflows, reduces errors, and democratizes coding. T5, originally designed for text-to-text tasks, and CodeT5, tailored for code intelligence, form the foundation of the robust text-to-code generation system. Through extensive mixed precision training, XLA compiler optimization, and distributed techniques, the model performance could be maximized. The MBPP dataset encompasses a wide range of Python programming problems, enabling our models to learn and generalize across various coding scenarios. We’ve developed utility functions and custom training loops to facilitate efficient data loading, model configuration, and training management. Assessments across various prediction tasks reveal the models’ effectiveness in generating precise and functional code snippets from natural language inputs. Practical applications of this research include integration into Integrated Development Environments (IDEs) for real-time code suggestions, educational tools for programming instruction, and assistance in maintaining and refactoring legacy codebases. Our work underscores the transformative potential of natural language-to-code generation by demonstrating the performance of this model where it could be understood code quality is outstanding, as evidenced by the performance metrics. A BLEU score of 0.4 indicates the model’s strong ability to produce high-quality code

Author Keywords: MBPP (Mostly Basic Python Programming) benchmark datasets

articleTitle: Enhancing Web Security For Threat Detection Through Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This article introduces a malware detection system based on deep learning, which focuses on malware classification in executable files. Instead of traditional methods, this system emphasizes static analysis between dangerous and harmless files. This requires a 1D-CNN, which is apt for analyzing portable executable files. Static analysis is critical because it detects features in the executable header, thus being a safer method compared to dynamic detection methods, which require specific environments, like virtual machines. The system is integrated into an online platform with a user-friendly web interface, thus easily accessible for users. Extensive comparisons with state-of-the-art models on three very different datasets show the excellence of this approach and establish a reliable, efficient, and practical solution for file executable identification. The presented system ensures speed and precision, providing an interesting point of advancement in malware detection toward easy deployment and use in real time for protection against malicious threats.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning Approach for Identifying LLM-Generated Text
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: In recent years, advancements in natural language processing (NLP) and machine learning have greatly improved the capabilities and accuracy of text detection systems. This has led to more efficient and precise solutions. This research focuses on developing an advanced language model tailored for text detection tasks, attaining a notable accuracy rate of 99.47%. The model utilizes cutting-edge transformer-based architectures, renowned for their capability to comprehend and analyse intricate patterns in textual data. A pre-trained language model was refined using a meticulously selected dataset, encompassing diverse. This careful selection of data allows the model to generalize effectively across various contexts, ensuring reliable performance even in challenging and unpredictable scenarios. During the training phase, key data preprocessing steps were used to transform raw text into a structured format appropriate for model analysis. These steps included tokenization, normalization, and vectorization. The model's performance was thoroughly evaluated using metrics like accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, demonstrating that it significantly outperforms conventional text detection methods, achieving groundbreaking results in the field. The practical applications of this model are far-reaching, covering areas such as automated content moderation, plagiarism detection, and information retrieval. For instance, social media platforms and online communities can benefit from real-time detection and removal of harmful or inappropriate content. In academic and professional settings, the model plays a key role in plagiarism detection, ensuring the originality of submitted work. Furthermore, by integrating this model into search engines and digital libraries, the relevance and precision of retrieved information can be enhanced, helping users access accurate and pertinent data more efficiently. This research underscores the vast potential of advanced NLP models in tackling complex issues related to text detection, highlighting the importance of continued progress in NLP and machine learning for building more reliable, efficient, and robust text processing systems.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approach to Snake Species Identification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Snake species identification is always challenging but is becoming increasingly intractable by the increasing diversity in snake species. This implies that the traditional methods of identification that heavily rely on the subjective estimates of the appearance can lead to potential inaccuracy in identifying such species. The present study puts forward a deep learning system applied to the identification of snake species, using CNNs and advanced image processing techniques. Our approach involves comprehensive data collection and preprocessing, followed by segmentation using YOLOv8s to accurately isolate snakes in images. Feature extraction is performed using MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetB0, while classification is achieved through various machine learning algorithms. Notably, an ensemble method combining multiple classifiers yields an impressive accuracy of 94%. The results clearly indicate the success of our approach to the automation of classification of snake species, which therefore contributes to better management practices and better public health initiatives on snake-bite prevention.

articleTitle: Optimizing the Longevity of Wireless Sensor Networks: A Comprehensive and Adaptive Energy-Efficient Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive method aimed at extending the operational lifetime of wireless sensor networks (WSNs) by optimizing energy consumption and improving network efficiency. A novel energy-aware routing protocol combined with duty cycling and data aggregation techniques is been introduced here Results from extensive simulations demonstrate significant improvements in network lifetime, data transmission efficiency, and overall performance.

articleTitle: Multi-label Emotion Classification using modified Sequential Deep Learning Architecture for Speech Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: In recent years, audio classification has gained significant attention due to its wide range of applications, particularly in the field of Speech Emotion Recognition (SER). Our paper presents a unique approach to multi-label audio classification based on emotion using a modified Sequential Deep Learning architecture, applied to a combined dataset of TESS, RAVDESS, SAVEE, and CREMA-D datasets. Our model employs SoftMax to obtain multi-class probabilities, which are then used to calculate evaluation metrics and uncertainties. Additionally, we explore the performance of our model across various emotion categories, demonstrating its robustness and versatility. Our model used Dropout Layers after every Layer in the architecture to decrease the overfitting and increase the accuracy. Comprehensive experiments show that our model achieves state-of-the-art results in multi-label classification, outperforming previous methods. The method also extensively evaluates the model’s performance.

articleTitle: IoT Intrusion: Detection Methods and Mitigation Strategies
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: In the age of revolutionized concepts of smart homes, offices, cities, industries, vehicles, the Internet of Things (IoT) devices play an integral role in collecting data, network for communication and cloud for processing and storage. Each of these layers of IoT are vulnerable to attacks, predominantly due to the leverages IoT requires in terms of storage, processing. Hence, there arises demand to secure IoT by detecting the intrusion in time and formulate mitigation to safeguard the devices and protect the data be it personal or commercial. This study presents IoT Intrusion Detection Methods like Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) methods at varying accuracies and mitigation strategies to bypass attacks and safeguard the network as well as devices within the network. This study summarizes various approaches in place for both detection and mitigation that can form the basis for future studies.

articleTitle: Optimizing FAANG Stock Forecasting: The Power of Feature Engineering and LSTM in Financial Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The unprecedented growth and market capitalization of the FAANG stocks - Facebook, Amazon, Apple, Netflix, and Google (Alphabet) - have mushroomed into the pay-off race of the leaders of the global financial market. Stock price volatility prediction attracts the focus of the investors and analysts in the pursuit of profit maximization relying on market movements. In order to enhance the precision of stock price predictions for FAANG companies, other more intricate methods for feature engineering are also coupled together with LSTM neural networks. Stock price dynamic intricacies are being reflected by the model using the complete set of financial indicators, predictive analytics, and market sentiment data as features. The work showed a phenomenal application of LSTM networks in the analysis and prediction of stock price trends compared to the classic methods on the sequential-by-nature front dealing with long dependencies. It is actually possible to build a strong base of data enabling the detection of such elusive trends in the performances of FAANG stocks and technical indicators, sentiment analysis, or economic metrics, for instance, thereby getting into working order for LSTM modeling. Results from experiments show the method provides better accuracy and reliability than conventional machine learning models, thus collecting valuable insights for certain financial-forecasting purposes. The paper serves as a demonstration illustrates how feature engineering and LSTM might be combined to improve predicting financial markets and provides one solution for investors, financial analysts, and policymakers who look to make informed investment decisions.

articleTitle: Automated Descriptive Audio Generation for Visually Impaired Individuals: A Framework Integrating Object Detection, Emotion Analysis, and Speech Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This study introduces an automated framework aimed at enhancing video accessibility for visually impaired individuals by generating descriptive audio. Utilizing advanced tools such as PySceneDetect for extracting keyframes, YOLOv8 for detecting and classifying objects, and DeepFace for analyzing emotional expressions, the system identifies key visual elements and emotional contexts within videos. Detailed captions are created using the BLIP model and are subsequently transformed into natural and customizable audio using ParlerTTS. The resulting descriptive audio is synchronized with the original video through tools like MoviePy and PyDub. This integrated solution provides an efficient, scalable, and automated method to make video content more accessible, enabling visually impaired users to better interpret and enjoy visual media.

articleTitle: Olympic Games Analysis and Visualization for Medal Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The Olympics is an international sporting event with over 200 countries participating in various competitions. Athletes from different countries compete and make their countries proud of their sporting excellence. Despite their huge populations, many of the most populous nations do not win many Olympic medals. The main purpose of this white paper is to use Python to analyze the Olympics dataset, compare the overall performance of each country, and evaluate each country’s contribution to the Olympics. These analyzes provide greater insight into each nation’s performance at the Olympic Games over the years and help athletes quickly analyze their own and their competitors’ performance.
