This paper uses exploratory data analysis techniques to compare the performance of different countries and their contribution to the Olympic Games. Various dimensions of the Olympics dataset are visualized to provide a country’s status in the Olympics, help underperforming countries produce quality athletes, and improve their performance in the Olympics.

articleTitle: Identification of Hair and Scalp Diseases by Machine Learning Based Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Diagnosing hair and scalp diseases has traditionally required lengthy manual examination by dermatologists. Individual machine learning models have shown promise but often fall short in handling the complex variability of dermatological conditions. This project proposes an ensemble model that combines Convolutional Neural Networks (Convolutional NN) and Random Forest (RF) algorithms to improve accuracy and reliability. The Convolutional NN extracts intricate image features from scalp and hair data, while the RF classifier refines these insights, minimizing overfitting and enhancing classification of non-linear patterns. This combined approach leverages Convolutional NN’s feature extraction capabilities and RF's robust classification to deliver more balanced, generalized predictions. Trained on a diverse dataset of conditions like alopecia, psoriasis, and healthy hair, the model achieves higher diagnostic accuracy than single-model solutions. A user-friendly interface also provides an accessible tool for patients and professionals, supporting early detection, proactive care, and better treatment outcomes

articleTitle: Smart waste management system using AR and IoT with AI
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The rapid urbanization and industrialization of cities have heightened the demand for efficient and sustainable waste management systems. Traditional methods struggle with inefficiencies, resulting in environmental pollution, resource wastage, and health hazards. This study proposes a smart waste management system that leverages the Internet of Things (IoT), Augmented Reality (AR), and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to address these challenges. IoT sensors embedded in waste bins provide real-time monitoring of fill levels, while AR applications assist waste management personnel in visualizing bin statuses and optimizing collection routes. AI algorithms analyze historical and real-time data to predict waste generation patterns, classify waste, and recommend efficient collection routes. The system enhances operational efficiency, reduces fuel consumption, and promotes sustainable waste management practices. The integration of these technologies aims to create a scalable, adaptable solution for urban waste management, contributing to environmental sustainability and supporting the development of smarter cities.

articleTitle: Image To Text Description Platform For Yakshagana Images By Detecting Crown Using CNN
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This research called "Yakshakatha – Image to Text Platform for Yakshagana Images." It employs deep learning to classify crowns in Yakshagana Kirita using CNN classification. Yakshagana is a traditional South Indian art form, well known for its intricate costumes and headgear, posing specific challenges in identifying and classifying crowns. The system aims to classify various Kirita styles and provide detailed descriptions of the respective Yakshagana characters, or Vesha, offering valuable cultural and symbolic insights. The model was trained on a self-labelled dataset of Yakshagana images and used convolutional and pooling layers to capture fine details in crown designs. It achieved an impressive accuracy of 99%, ensuring precise identification and classification. Real-time predictions for the input images are made, which have predetermined mappings and description content for recognized characters. The system employs Google Gemini AI, in order to enrich the text description of the image by integrating cultural background. The responsive interface is provided for users on the image upload, real-time result, and enriched visual feedback using annotated output. This project combines modern image recognition with rich cultural content to preserve and promote the traditional heritage of Yakshagana. It will help the users to understand and appreciate the vibrancy of this art form.

articleTitle: Transforming Healthcare: A Comprehensive Review of AI-Powered Chatbots Impact and Applications in Healthcare Services
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot integration in healthcare has enormous potential to improve patient care delivery, expedite administrative procedures, and improve overall health outcomes. This implementation is not without difficulties, though. This analysis examines the state of AI chatbots in the healthcare industry, emphasizing important problems and solutions. Technical obstacles that block interoperability and data transmission include the lack of standardization in healthcare data formats and the limited comprehension of Natural Language. Further obstacles include ethical issues with AI-driven decision-making, regulatory compliance, and certification. Furthermore, integration with clinical workflows and user acceptability are essential for a successful implementation. Not with standing these difficulties, AI chatbots have many advantages, such as increased patient interaction, individualized treatment, and increased operational effectiveness. Healthcare companies may use AI chatbots to change healthcare delivery and enhance patient outcomes by tackling these problems together, coming up with creative solutions, and enforcing ethical standards.

articleTitle: Local Language Handwritten Character Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The idea of the proposed methodology is to develop an efficient system that can recognize handwritten Kannada characters, a language whose script is quite complex. It makes use of feature extraction by using CNN in conjunction with a hybrid SVM-CNN approach in classification to overcome handwriting variation. The SVM-CNN hybrid takes the strength of CNN pattern recognition and complements it with SVM classification; Also, the preprocessing would include the binarization of images and noise removal to have more qualitative data, hence significantly improving the recognition process as a whole. This holistic approach provides greater accuracy and robustness in recognition of regional languages in further digitization efforts focused on document digitization applications, automated systems, and educational tool sets for an inclusive digital practice.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Classification and Detection of Position using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Brain tumor classification is essential for tumor evaluation and choosing appropriate therapeutic strategies, as it is based on types of tumors. Although there are several imaging methods to identify brain tumors, Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is often more preferable because of the improved quality of the image and the usage of a non-ionizing radiation. Recently, Deep Learning (DL) has demonstrated impressive performance on segmentation and classification tasks. This was achieved by creating a Convolution Neural Network (CNN) that extracts features through the process of backpropagation with essential components. The main objectives of this work were to create a CNN for the diagnostic and segmentation purposes of a brain tumor in MRI images. The proposed classification model is developed using CNN architecture to categorize MRI images into 4 different classes such as meningioma, glioma, pituitary adenoma and non-tumor images. A U-Net architecture has been used for the segmentation model, which helps identify and separate tumor areas in MRI scans metrics. In order to test the reliability of these models, we used publicly available data, achieving impressive outcomes with a classification accuracy of 95% and a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 93.98% for segmentation. By using the classification and the segmentation approaches, we created a web application for brain tumor categorization and localization in real time. These are promising in regards to being adapted into clinically relevant models during the diagnosis and treatment of brain tumors.

articleTitle: Deepfake Image Detection using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Deepfake images are generated by modifying existing visuals and are frequently exploited in harmful ways. When executed proficiently, these images can be almost indistinguishable from authentic ones. The increasing development of deep learning techniques has largely fueled the increase in deepfake content. While numerous techniques are available for creating deepfake images, the most commonly employed are GANs and autoencoders. This paper presents a way to make deepfake detection more accurate by using a combination of the YOLOv8 model and a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN). YOLOv8 extracts spatial details from the images, while the RNN identifies temporal patterns and subtle irregularities across image frames, signaling potential manipulation. This methodology presents an efficient solution for identifying deepfake images and reducing their misuse.

articleTitle: Key Aggregation in Trusted Execution for Multi-Query Privacy in Cloud Computing with Enhancing Data Privacy
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The critical challenge of maintaining privacy in multi-query data processing environments, is a major concern, increasingly prevalent in the era of big data. The paper introduces the Key Aggregation in Trusted Execution for Multi-Query Privacy (KATE-MQP) architecture, a novel framework designed to securely handle, process, and analyze data across multiple queries while ensuring stringent privacy preservation. Utilizing differential privacy for key aggregation, the KATE-MQP model represents a significant advancement in the field. Methodologically, the architecture combines Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) with sophisticated key management. The standout result of the KATE-MQP model is its ability to achieve an increased key aggregation accuracy by 40% while enhancing data privacy, as compared to existing models. Quantitatively, the model demonstrates a marked improvement in processing efficiency as the load increases, demonstrating its scalability. These results underscore the KATE-MQP architecture's potential as a scalable and efficient solution for secure data processing in various applications, from healthcare to finance, where data privacy and integrity are paramount.

articleTitle: Comparative study of Machine Learning, Deep Learning and Bayesian Models on the ORL Faces Dataset for Effectual Face Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This study compares face recognition performance between machine learning, deep learning, and probabilistic reasoning models. On the ORL dataset from Kaggle, the Machine Learning (ML) model (support vector machine (SVM)) achieved a recognition accuracy of 96.25.%, The Deep Learning (DL) model convolutional neural network (CNN) achieved a recognition accuracy of 99.99.% and a Probabilistic (PR) model Bayesian network attained an accuracy of 90.%. This analysis emphasizes CNN’s superior accuracy in face recognition, especially on large-scale datasets, while also illuminating the comparatively limited effectiveness of Bayesian Networks with PCA and SVM for dimensionality reduction and classification.

articleTitle: SpiralDrawNet: CNN-Driven Early Detection of Parkinson's Disease using Spiral Drawings for Accessible Healthcare Solution
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Millions of people worldwide suffer with Parkinson's disease (PD), a neurological condition. For PD to be effectively managed and treated, early identification is essential. This study investigates the use of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in combination with spiral drawings, a straightforward and non-invasive technique, for Parkinson's disease identification. Spiral drawings from both PD patients and non-PD patients make up the research dataset. Digital images are created by processing these sketches. These spiral designs are used to create and train a CNN architecture that divides them into PD and non-PD categories. To increase the model's resilience, a variety of data augmentation strategies are used. Experimental results demonstrate promising performance in PD detection, with the CNN achieving high accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. The study highlights the potential of utilizing spiral drawings as a cost-effective and accessible tool for early PD screening. Additionally, the CNN-based approach shows the feasibility of automated PD diagnosis, offering a scalable solution for healthcare professionals.

articleTitle: A CNN-LSTM Framework for Real-Time Human Action Recognition in Video Sequences
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced framework for action recognition in video sequences, leveraging the combined strengths of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to capture both spatial and temporal dimensions of human activities. The framework processes video input by extracting individual frames and analyzing spatial features through CNNs to determine "what" actions occur in each frame. These extracted features are then passed to an LSTM network, which models the temporal dynamics, allowing the system to understand "how" actions unfold over time. Real-time processing capabilities are enabled through OpenCV, making this approach suitable for applications requiring immediate feedback and dynamic response. The model is trained on a diverse dataset encompassing a range of action classes, achieving high accuracy in recognizing activities from simple gestures to complex behaviors. This CNN-LSTM architecture demonstrates broad applicability across various domains: it can identify abnormal behavior in surveillance settings, enable gesture-based control in human-computer interaction, and analyze athletic performance in sports. By integrating CNNs and LSTMs, this framework enhances automated video analysis capabilities and underscores the potential of deep learning to interpret complex human actions in real-world scenarios. This work represents a significant step forward in video-based action recognition, paving the way for more intelligent, responsive, and robust systems.

articleTitle: Recurrent Neural Networks for Real-Time Position Estimation of Robotic Arm End-Effector Coordinates
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Robotic arm manipulators find application in fields like manufacturing, construction, and automation due to their inherent ability to perform accurate and repetitive operations. These manipulators consist of multiple joints and links, enabling complex, multi-directional motions. However, accurately determining end-effector positions poses significant challenges due to the complexity of kinematic calculations. Due to the difficulty in estimating the formula to get to this solution, we have proposed the addition of a Deep Learning Model based Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) to predict the end-effectors X, Y, and Z positions according to the input of the 6 joints of the robotic arm. A robust dataset is generated using the Denavit-Hartenberg (D-H) parameterization for randomly sampled joint configurations. The RNN model is trained and validated over 50 epochs using a dense layer with 100 units and subsequently evaluated using three key metrics: Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and R-Squared Score. Enhancements to the analysis of the models performance will include confusion matrices and Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curves to assess the accuracy of each category. Finally, the developed model predicts the end-effector for any user input with high accuracy, providing an efficient and reliable solution for real-time kinematic computations in robotic applications.

articleTitle: Assessing University Students' Mental Health through Ensemble Machine Learning: The Role of Academic, Social, and Lifestyle Factors on Depression, Anxiety, and Future Insecurity
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Student mental health is becoming an increasingly important problem at academic institutions around the world. The mental health of university students is examined in connection to a number of demographic, academic, and lifestyle variables. Examining the efficacy of students' stress-relieving behaviours was another aspect of the study. Results point to a considerable relationship between students' mental health issues and their lifestyle choices, the amount of work they have to do in school, and their bad experiences on campus.Utilizing algorithms like Random Forest, Decision Tree, XGBoost, and CatBoost, the research focuses on identifying key academic, social, and lifestyle factors that contribute to mental health challenges. The results highlight the predictive accuracy and robustness of ensemble models, offering actionable insights for student mental health interventions.

articleTitle: Comparative study of Federated learning models in a cross-silo scenario with Flower framework
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Federated learning in a cross-silo scenario’s encounters obstacles such as uneven performance across many medical fields, class imbalance, and data privacy concerns. These problems are difficult for traditional centralized machine learning techniques to solve while preserving the efficacy of the model and the confidentiality of the data. This study aims to examine various local training strategies in a privacy-preserving framework, address class imbalance issues, and evaluate the performance of federated learning models in several healthcare data sets. The flower framework is used to apply federated learning in three healthcare datasets: heart disease, breast cancer, and diabetes. Techniques such as SMOTE, ADASYN, and upsampling are used to reduce class imbalance. Both logistic regression and neural networks were used for local training. Various communication rounds were used to assess model performance using accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and loss measures. Across all datasets, the federated learning models performed better with more communication rounds. After 200 rounds, the breast cancer model had the best results, scoring 95% accuracy, 96% precision, 96% recall, and 96% F1 score. Accuracy rates for the diabetes and heart disease models were 80% and 81%, respectively. In local training, neural networks typically performed better than logistic regression. This study demonstrates the performance of federated learning in healthcare applications across several domains.

articleTitle: Review of Lightweight Cryptographic Algorithm: NIST Requirement and Practical Implementation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The technological development has increased the requirement for robust security measures to protect the information. Many new security concerns arise as a result of the transition from high-end devices, like desktop computers, servers, and laptops, to smaller devices with limited resources. A number of these devices, such as smart cards, RFID tags, and wireless sensors, require secure ways of storing, accessing, and transmitting vital data. The primary objective of lightweight cryptography is to provide cryptographic algorithms that are tailored for these kinds of limited environments. This paper discusses the principles of lightweight cryptography, the requirements set forth by NIST for these algorithms, and their practical implementations on platforms like FPGAs.

articleTitle: Semi-supervised Learning - An Alternative to Traditional Breast Cancer Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Breast cancer continues to create diagnostic challenges due to its overlapping and diverse characteristics, complicating the diagnosis. This study evaluates various cases for each stage of preprocessing and optimization techniques in Supervised Learning (SL) and Semi-Supervised Learning (SSL) to attain optimal predictive performance. Nine machine learning classifiers were utilized for both SL and SSL Models for training and testing on the Wisconsin Diagnostic Cancer Dataset using the following algorithms: 1) Logistic Regression (LR), 2) Gaussian Naive Bayes (GNB), 3) Linear-SVM, 4) RBF-SVM, 5) DT, 6) RF, 7) XGBoost, 8) Gradient Boosting (GB), and 9) K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN).This process incorporated feature extraction techniques, including Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), Feature Agglomeration, and feature selection through Regularization, employing both L2 and Bayesian methods. For hyperparameter optimization, a comprehensive approach Stratified K-fold and nested cross-validation was adopted and the Model has performed well by acheiving an accuracy of 99% compare to SL, which has showcased that SSL can be an alternative approach for sl when the labeled data is expensive or high computational resources are required.

articleTitle: A Unified Fog Computing Architecture for Next-Generation Smart City Traffic and Crime Management
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The rapid growth of urbanization has led to a surge in demand for smart city systems that can efficiently manage resources and ensure safety. This paper delves into the design and simulation of a Smart City System that leverages Fog Computing. Fog Computing involves distributing computation and storage resources across devices located at the network edge. The system integrates a diverse range of sensors, including surveillance cameras, VPR (Vehicle Plate Recognition) cameras, and audio sensors, strategically deployed across different city areas. These sensors monitor traffic, detect anomalies, and promptly provide real-time alerts. The Fog architecture enhances system responsiveness by processing data closer to its source, thereby reducing latency and bandwidth consumption. To model and simulate the interaction between various Fog devices, cloud resources, and edge-based applications, we employ CloudSim, a cloud simulation tool. By meticulously mapping different application modules to devices based on their capabilities, we simulate the execution of smart city applications, such as video capture, traffic detection, and audio alarm triggering. The results show the possibility of employing Fog Computing for building an efficient, scalable, and responsive system for a smart city. Fog computing has the potential to significantly impact large urban areas by processing data at the edge, thereby reducing latency and bandwidth consumption.

articleTitle: Harnessing Disruptive Technologies in Education: The Role of AI, VR/AR, Blockchain, IoT, and Adaptive Learning Platforms
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Traditional learning models are being reshaped by the quick adoption of disruptive technologies in education, which presents new chances for individualized, engaging, and effective learning experiences. In order to improve educational results, this article examines the revolutionary potential of five important technologies: blockchain, the Internet of Things, virtual reality and augmented reality, artificial intelligence and machine learning, and adaptive learning platforms. Virtual reality and augmented reality offer immersive settings that improve engagement and recall of complicated concepts, while AI-driven systems are reinventing adaptive learning by customizing information to individual learning styles and requirements. Blockchain technology provides decentralized, safe solutions for data integrity, trust building, and academic record management. While adaptive learning systems further personalize education by assessing student performance data to enhance curriculum delivery, IoT allows linked classrooms, which improve resource accessibility and engagement. In order to provide insights into how these technologies might be used to build an educational environment that is more inclusive and prepared for the future, this study looks at the distinct contributions of each technology, their synergies, and the difficulties involved in integrating them. The results demonstrate the way these technologies have the potential to significantly enhance learning outcomes, accessibility, and student engagement in a variety of teaching contexts.

articleTitle: A Performance Comparison Between Machine Learning, Deep Learning, and Bayesian Approaches for COVID-19 Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic emphasizes the critical need for rapid and reliable diagnostic procedures to improve infection detection and prevention. This study compares Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning(DL) and probabilistic graphical models (PGMs) for predicting COVID-19 infection using a publicly available dataset. ML models such as Support Vector Machine(SVM), Random Forest(RF), Decision Tree(DT), K-Nearest Neighbour(KNN), Multi Layer Perceptron(MLP) and Voting Classifier(VC) with Synthetic Minority Over sampling Technique (SMOTE) attained an accuracy of 98.9%. The Deep Neural Network (DNN) attained 97.88% accuracy and Bayesian Network(BN)implemented using Probabilistic Graphical Models in Python(PGMPY) achieved 96 % accuracy. Despite lower accuracy, BN helps in complex diagnostic tasks. It also demonstrates the power of ensemble ML and DL models. Therefore these results reflect the advantages attained from ensemble ML,DL and BN models in terms of flexibility and the ability of each approach to solve complex diagnostic problems and tasks, as represented by the predictive modeling of COVID-19 cases.

articleTitle: LIVES: XAI-based Secure UAV Communication Framework for Essential Items Delivery
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The application of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) for securely delivering essential items during extreme conditions includes numerous challenges, particularly in ensuring identification of potential threats. To solve this challenge, we propose a strong framework that makes use of Boosting algorithms, with a particular focus on XGBoost to enhance attack classification in UAV-based delivery systems. The XGBoost model achieved an accuracy of 93%, a precision of 0.9312, a recall of 0.9311, and an F1 score of 0.9283 , which makes it a highly suitable model for security of UAVs. Explainable AI (XAI) is used to further enhance classification including SHAP and LIME to identify the most influential features, such as the barometer and battery levels. Our framework provides a comprehensive solution for secure UAV-based deliveries. The experimental results proves the effectiveness of the proposed model which shows its potential for real-life applications.

articleTitle: Innovative AI Solutions for Multi-Modal Content Generation
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: To overcome contemporary constraints in the field of AI-driven art generation, the AI ImageGen project offers a robust, intuitive framework for creating images utilizing different AI models. Utilizing a variety of cutting-edge models integrated through the Hugging Face API, this web application enables users to generate distinctive, high-quality photos by entering bespoke text prompts. AI ImageGen, which is built with React for the frontend and Node.js for the backend, provides a smooth user experience with a simplified UI thanks to Ant Design. In addition to creating photographs, users may efficiently manage their outputs by viewing, downloading, and deleting their creations. AI methods for creating images have historically advanced quickly, but many platforms still only provide a limited amount of customisation and model selection flexibility.By letting users select from a variety of models, AI ImageGen closes this gap and promotes output diversity and creativity. In order to facilitate the creation of AI-based art by a wider audience, this project also attempts to enhance the general usability of AI tools for nontechnical users. With its adaptable, multi-model methodology and emphasis on a seamless user experience, AI ImageGen is a cutting-edge solution in the rapidly expanding field of AI art generating.

articleTitle: Bridging the Communication Gap: An Improved Real-Time Indian Sign Language Translation with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Indian Sign Language (ISL) is the primary mode of communication for the Deaf and Hard-of-Hearing (DHH) community in India. However, communication barriers persist due to limited public awareness of ISL. This work presents a real-time gesture recognition system that translates ISL gestures into text and speech, facilitating interaction between ISL users and non-signers. The system employs Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for spatial feature extraction and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for capturing temporal patterns in sequential gesture data. A diverse dataset, incorporating variations in hand movements, facial expressions, and body posture, enhances model accuracy. The integration of deep learning techniques allows continuous performance improvement. This solution fosters inclusivity by bridging the communication gap in public spaces, educational institutions, and workplaces. The proposed system offers a scalable, cost-effective approach to improving accessibility and social integration for the DHH community.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of Flood Image Segmentation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Effective segmentation of flood-affected areas must be done for effective disaster management and recovery planning. This paper conducts a performance comparison of four different segmentation techniques on flood-area images. Techniques adopted in this work are region growing, active contour, histogram, and K-means clustering. K-means algorithm is based on Machine Learning technique. Further, consistency verification is applied on segmented images. The original flood image is segmented first using four methods. Generated masks are compared with a ground truth mask. The Score value is computed using a confusion matrix. Difference maps are further generated to visualize segmentation results. It provides valuable insights into the strengths and weaknesses of each method that can be used to select optimal approaches for the analysis of flood areas. Score is considered the performance metric used to assess the performance of various techniques. Machine learning based K-means segmentation along with consistency verification outperforming than other techniques.

articleTitle: A Survey on Innovation in Medical Science using Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This paper examines into the transformative impact of technological innovations in the medical field, highlighting how advancements have revolutionized patient care, diagnostics, and overall healthcare management. The incorporation of advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), telemedicine, and robotics, has not only enhanced the precision and efficiency of medical interventions but also broadened access to healthcare services. By automating diagnostic processes, improving surgical techniques, and enabling real-time remote consultations, these innovations are reshaping the landscape of modern healthcare. The paper examines the current state of these technologies, discusses the challenges associated with their implementation including ethical concerns, data privacy issues, and the cost of adoption and evaluates their potential in future medical advancements. Additionally, the paper explores emerging trends in medical technology, offering insights into how these innovations may continue to evolve and contribute to improving healthcare outcomes, patient experience, and the overall efficiency of healthcare systems worldwide.

articleTitle: Deep Learning in Forensic Sketch Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: When images of suspects are not accessible, forensic sketch analysis plays a crucial role in criminal investigations by giving investigators a visual representation of the subject. These sketches have typically been manually matched to databases or mugshots, which is a laborious and prone to human error process. This study investigates the use of cutting-edge deep learning methods to improve and automate forensic sketch recognition. In order to automate and improve sketch-to-photo recognition using public datasets, this work investigates sophisticated deep-learning techniques such as autoencoders, GANs, and CNNs. PCA and t-SNE are examples of dimensionality reduction algorithms that enhance feature representation and visualization. The outcomes indicate how well these models work to increase matching accuracy, providing law enforcement with a quicker and more dependable tool and highlighting AI’s potential to enhance criminal investigations and public safety.

articleTitle: An Empirical Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for Stroke Risk Assessment with Explainable AI
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Stroke has significant socioeconomic effects, particularly in low- and middle-income nations, and is a major cause of mortality and disability worldwide. This study applies machine learning models to predict stroke, leveraging clinical and demographic data to highlight those who may be at risk. We applied a range of models, including Random Forest, XGBoost, Gradient Boosting, and Neural Networks, after comprehensive data preprocessing. Among these, Random Forest achieved the highest accuracy (98.87%) and ROC AUC (1.0), making it highly effective for stroke risk prediction. We improved transparency in healthcare applications by emphasizing the relevance of individual risk factors in forecasts using LIME for model interpretability.. These findings support the use of ensemble models and explainable AI for reliable, interpretable stroke prediction, paving the way for preventive healthcare.

articleTitle: A Real-time Sign Language Recognition System using MediaPipe and Random Forest Classifier combining with Text-to-Speech Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This research study introduces a real-time sign language detection system utilizing hand gestures, specifically developed to bridge the communication gap for deaf and hard-of-hearing individuals. The system employs advanced computer vision techniques, utilizing MediaPipe for accurate hand tracking and landmark detection, extracting key features such as fingertip and palm positions. These features are normalized to address variations in hand size and orientation, ensuring consistent input for classification. A Random Forest Classifier (RFC), trained on a labeled dataset of gestures, processes the data to achieve reliable recognition. The system offers dual feedback mechanisms: real-time visual text overlays on live video streams and Text-to-Speech (TTS) output, making it intuitive and user-friendly. Iterative training and out-of-bag error monitoring enhance model performance, ensuring seamless functionality across devices ranging from mobile phones to larger systems. Motivated by the need for inclusivity, this solution enables effortless communication in both social and professional contexts. By leveraging AI-driven approaches, the system provides an accessible and efficient tool for promoting understanding and interaction, advancing assistive technologies for deaf and hard-of-hearing communities. This work represents a significant step toward creating more inclusive communication solutions.

articleTitle: A Decision Support System for Detection, Analysis and Classification of Paddy Plant Diseases
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Paddy crop health is increasingly threatened by diseases that lead to significant yield loss, making manual inspection insufficient due to its time-consuming and unreliable nature. This paper proposes an end-to-end solution integrating an Android app and web interface for user interaction, a machine learning algorithm for disease classification, and cloud-based infrastructure for data storage and analysis. The system employs image processing and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to analyze paddy leaf images, targeting four diseases: blast, bacterial leaf blight, brown spots, and tungro. Two models were developed—one to identify healthy crops and another to classify diseases. Farmers can capture and upload crop images via the Android app, which are then classified using a Google Cloud function. The system also stores telemetry data, such as location and images, for further analysis, including identifying disease hotspots and providing management recommendations. The app displays the nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) location and contact details using OpenStreetMap. With 95% accuracy in detecting healthy crops and 99% in disease classification, this solution aims to improve crop yield through early disease detection and timely interventions.

articleTitle: Mitigating Biases in Dermatological Diagnosis through GAN Augmentation and Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Skin conditions affect individuals of all skin tones, yet biases in dermatological diagnosis disproportionately impact those with darker skin, leading to significant healthcare disparities. This paper proposes a comprehensive solution that integrates advanced data preprocessing, Generative Adverserial Network (GAN) augmentation, and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models to mitigate these biases. The initial phase involves meticulous preprocessing of diverse dermatological image datasets, ensuring broad coverage of skin tones. Images are standardized, noise is removed, and critical features are preserved for accurate classification. To address data imbalance, particularly for underrepresented skin tones, a GAN with spectral normalization generates synthetic images of dark skin lesions, enriching the dataset and enhancing model generalization. The preprocessed and augmented dataset is used to train three CNN architectures are ResNet50, NASNetLarge, and InceptionResNetV2, each fine-tuned to optimize performance. Class weights handle imbalances, and an ensemble approach improves classification accuracy, particularly in detecting challenging conditions like melanoma across all skin tones. This combined approach of GAN augmentation and CNN-based classification offers a promising path toward more equitable dermatological diagnostics.

articleTitle: Smart Mood Detection: Real-Time Emotion Analysis for Human-Computer Interaction Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: A convolutional neural network (CNN)-based face emotion recognition system that analyzes human emotions in real-time, including happy, sorrow, rage, and surprise, is described. Existing approaches often struggle with accurately recognizing subtle or complex emotions due to limited feature extraction capabilities and the need for large, diverse training datasets. Additionally, they face challenges in adapting to real-world conditions, such as variations in lighting, angles, and occlusions. In order to improve the model's generalizability, the proposed research used a preprocessing pipeline that included gray scale conversion, scaling, normalization, and augmentation techniques including rotation and flipping on a labeled and balanced dataset of facial photos. Dropout and regularization techniques were used to reduce over fitting, and the CNN architecture was meticulously adjusted to maximize speed. High accuracy and resilience across emotion categories are demonstrated by preliminary results, indicating the model's potential for real-world uses in security surveillance, healthcare, and human-computer interaction.

articleTitle: YogaPose-8 : A Diverse Yoga Pose Dataset for Classification and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Proper identification of yoga-poses is important in ensuring safe and effective practice, yet most existing machine learning techniques often raise several data privacy concerns and face challenges in acquiring diverse datasets, particularly concerning data availability. Our study is the first to employ Flower Federated Learning for classifying eight distinct yoga-poses in a way that resolves these issues, by allowing multiple clients to train a shared model collaboratively without revealing personal information. This method leverages Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for feature extraction and combines knowledge from clients’ private datasets while ensuring confidentiality and improving data availability. We utilize a carefully curated dataset of 7442 images of eight poses, collected from users and various websites, to train our model. Our comprehensive training achieves an impressive accuracy of 99.2%, demonstrating the efficacy of federated learning. Our findings show that federated learning can preserve data privacy while delivering performance levels comparable to centralized models. Additionally, the federated architecture provides robustness against changes in data distribution across client devices. This research offers a novel approach to yoga-pose identification, paving the way for precise techniques that address both data privacy and availability concerns, and acting as a foundational step towards effective yoga-pose correction.

articleTitle: Text-to-Voice Conversion for Indic Languages
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The demand for sophisticated Text-to-Speech (TTS) systems is rising due to linguistic diversity, with Indic languages posing particular difficulties. Conventional text-to-speech (TTS) synthesis algorithms frequently fall short in capturing the rich expressiveness and subtle cultural nuances of Indic languages, resulting in an artificial voice output devoid of authentic prosody. By integrating the HiFi-GAN for high-fidelity voice cloning and the Tortoise TTS framework into a hybrid TTS architecture, this solution suggests a novel way to get beyond these restrictions. Allowing the system to pick up on and replicate the complex patterns and nuanced subtleties of Indic speech. High-fidelity waveforms are effectively synthesized from mel-spectrograms by the HiFi-GAN vocoder, while extremely expressive and natural-sounding speech waveforms are produced by the Tortoise TTS model, which is based on Denoising Diffusion Restoration Models. High-quality training data is ensured via a complex data processing pipeline that includes silence reduction, audio segmentation, and transcription filtering. The suggested system performs much better than current TTS systems on both Mean Opinion Score (MOS) and Comparative Mean Opinion Score (CMOS) according to extensive subjective evaluations.

articleTitle: Classification of Early Onset of Diabetes with Machine Learning, Deep Learning Algorithms, and Bayesian Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Diabetes is a chronic disease that cannot be permanently cured, making early detection critical. Our research utilized Data Mining, Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning, and Bayesian Networks to predict diabetes. We used the Pima Indian Diabetes Dataset (PIDD), which was obtained from the UCI ML Repository and contains data from 768 patients across nine distinct variables. Seven ML algorithms were applied to this dataset to predict diabetes, and we found that Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and AdaBoost (AB) performed well. Additionally, we explored BN to model probabilistic relationships between diabetes risk factors, which further contributed to prediction accuracy. We also developed Neural Networks (NN) with varying hidden layers and epochs, discovering that an NN with three hidden layers achieved an accuracy of 89.90%.

articleTitle: Live facial emotion detection and age-gender prediction using OpenCV and deep learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Facial emotion recognition (FER) is crucial in education, healthcare, marketing, and human-computer interaction. This paper reviews live FER systems employing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and OpenCV, integrating age and gender detection to improve accuracy and adaptability. While traditional FER methods focus on static images, human emotions are better analyzed through continuous video frames. By combining CNNs with long short-term memory (LSTM) networks, the approach captures both spatial and temporal features, enhancing real-time emotion classification.

articleTitle: Design of a Model for Early Detection of Abnormal Heart Rhythms and Its Severity in Electrocardiogrma Using Deep Learning Techinques
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: This work presents a deep learning method for evaluating the severity and early identification of irregular cardiac rhythms in electrocardiogram (ECG) readings. The model uses Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to accurately classify normal and pathological rhythms by extracting complex information from ECG data. Additionally, a regression model is used to evaluate the severity of irregular beats, giving physicians important information. The suggested model performs well in tasks involving both detection and severity assessment, according to evaluation using a sizable ECG dataset. Through the provision of a trustworthy mechanism for the preliminary diagnosis and treatment of cardiovascular illnesses, this research advances healthcare technology.

articleTitle: Healthy Life Expectancy (HALE) Analysis and Prediction using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Life expectancy serves as a major shift for policymakers and the healthcare sectors by enhancing the major need for humans in the society. In the last century life expectancy of countries has been measured more accurately than ever before due to better survey methods. These results have been statistically analyzed, and with methods including machine learning, trends have been analyzed to see what affects mortality and where human longevity is headed. We compare machine learning models to compare Healthy Life Expectancy, also known as HALE, across countries, and observe its relationship with socio-demographic factors.

articleTitle: Demand Prediction using AutoML Based Ensemble Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The integration of AutoML and ensemble techniques plays a pivotal role in enhancing demand forecasting by automating essential processes such as model selection, data cleaning, and hyperparameter tuning. These automated features streamline the machine-learning pipeline, significantly reducing the manual effort involved in model building and ensuring faster model deployment. By combining the outputs of multiple models through ensemble techniques, the approach leverages the strengths of each model, leading to improved accuracy and robustness in demand predictions. This system generates highly accurate demand estimates, which are crucial for optimizing operations like inventory management, resource allocation, and supply chain planning. Sectors like e-commerce, retail, and tourism, where demand fluctuations are common, can particularly benefit from such precise predictions. The automation also enables businesses to make well-informed decisions without needing in-depth expertise in machine learning, allowing for quicker responses to market dynamics. Incorporating real-time data is a key area for future development. This would allow for more dynamic forecasting that responds immediately to changes in consumer behavior or external factors, further improving the accuracy of predictions. Additionally, tailoring AutoML systems to address the unique challenges of different industries, such as considering sector-specific variables and data patterns, will make the technology even more effective. Overall, the combination of AutoML and ensemble techniques enhances decision-making by offering scalable, accurate, and efficient demand forecasting solutions across industries.

articleTitle: FMEA-Based Safety Analysis of Monocular Depth Estimation for Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Deploying monocular depth estimation systems in autonomous vehicles presents unique challenges, particularly in complex urban environments. This study conducts a comprehensive Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) focusing on autonomous vehicle behavior at urban intersections. We identify and categorize critical failure modes, their effects, and potential mitigation strategies by analyzing a single four-way intersection scenario under daylight conditions. The research systematically quantifies risks using established metrics, including depth accuracy and processing latency. Our findings reveal that the most critical failure modes occur during the intersection entry phase, with distance estimation errors and missed detections presenting the highest Risk Priority Numbers (RPNs). We establish safety thresholds and validation frameworks for intersection scenarios through detailed performance metrics and statistical analysis. This focused approach provides valuable insights for system designers and safety engineers, contributing to developing robust safety guidelines for monocular depth estimation systems.

articleTitle: Exploring an overview of machine learning techniques for identifying diabetes: A review
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Diabetes is among the most severe long-term complications of metabolic disease, typically arising from higher levels of blood sugar spurred on by either inadequate insulin synthesis or inappropriate insulin use by the body. Numerous health problems, including nerve damage, renal problems, and heart disease, may arise from it. Controlling diabetes and avoiding its complications requires proper treatment, which includes medication and lifestyle modifications. The goal of this review study is to highlight recent developments and problems in the area of diabetes identification by analysing lot of Machine Learning (ML) approaches. Conventional ML-based approaches are among the main categories into which the review divides current methodologies. We explore the techniques, guiding concepts, and noteworthy algorithms for each category, offering a thorough analysis of their advantages as well as suggestions for future research.

articleTitle: Hybrid CNN-GRU based Machine Vision Multimodal Deep Learning Model for Glaucoma Detection in Retinal Fundus Image
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: One of the most common and well-known conditions is glaucoma, but patients, especially those over 60, may lose their vision if the condition is left untreated or misdiagnosed. In the proposed work, we classify a picture as either healthy or glaucomatous using convolutional neural networks. The assessment of glaucomatous optic nerve and retinal damage may be achieved by structural evaluation using optical coherence tomography (OCT), and the degree of vision loss can be ascertained through functional visual field (VF) testing. In this work, we used a convolutional neural network (CNN) and a long short-term memory (LSTM) network to develop a multimodal deep learning model for glaucoma progression prediction. We used OCT scans, VF values, clinical, and demographic information from 89 glaucoma patients who saw five different physicians in a 12-month period. We showed that our novel generative model-based method can predict progression seven months ahead of time with the greatest AUC of 0.85. Moreover, the incorporation of artificial future images enabled the model to accurately forecast vision loss up to 8 months ahead of time with an AUC of 0.83, in contrast to the use of just structural (AUC = 0.69) or functional metrics (AUC = 0.71). The viability of using artificial follow-up OCT pictures to detect glaucoma development early is clarified by this study. As part of transfer learning, hyperparameters including the learning rate, optimizers, and activation function are changed throughout experimentation. The work offers practicing ophthalmologists an alternative point of view.

articleTitle: Credit Card Fraud Identification with ANN and LSTM based models
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: The past few years have seen a sharp escalation in the most concerning and widespread type of credit card theft, which has resulted in significant losses. [1] At the same time, security and authentication technology developments are encouraging because fraudsters are using more advanced methods, including card cloning, phishing, skimming, and data breaches. Among the above, many models Common methods such as LR, SVMs, Forest-based algorithms are also utilized, alongside LightGBM are applied for the purpose of fraud prediction. However, due to their respective deficiencies in handling huge datasets, abstracting hierarchical representations, and engineering new features, most of the above-mentioned models could not fare any better than the accuracy level of deep learning models like ANN. It is well known that ANN-based models require a significant amount of training over larger datasets in order to provide the best results, even if they have the added benefit of improving accuracy with improved performance. Since deep learning methods improve detection while adapting to evolving fraud patterns, the work incorporates them into the Credit card scam detection system. Within the end, The research presented here findings demonstrate that the fight against credit card fraud will need to include ongoing advancements in algorithms and data gathering techniques. The obtained results reveal that the classifiers perform more effective in the processed data than in the original data. From all the algorithms, the ANN-LSTM model presented the best results, attaining an accuracy, precision, recall, specificity and f1-score having values of 98%, 97.69%, 97.75%, 97.69% and 97.72% respectively.

articleTitle: Leveraging Machine Learning for Pattern-Based Detection of Respiratory Illnesses
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Lung sound analysis presents a promising, noninvasive, and potentially cost-effective approach for detecting respiratory diseases. This research aims to assess the feasibility of using lung sounds for pattern recognition and detection of various respiratory disorders, specifically by conducting an analysis of cough sounds. We review a range of recent studies that explore the use of deep learning models, machine learning algorithms, and feature extraction techniques in this context. These studies are categorized based on their methodologies, and their performance in accurately classifying lung sounds is discussed. Research findings highlight the significant diagnostic potential of lung sound analysis, demonstrating improved classification accuracies across various disease types. However, challenges such as data inconsistency, noise interference, and limited model generalizability remain. It captures the current state of lung sound analysis research in respiratory disease detection, offering insights that could drive future advancements in this critical field.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Menstrual Analysis of Stress and Mood in Indian Women
publicationTitle: 2025 International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Engineering (AIDE)
abstract: Women experience hormonal changes at several life stages, including menarche, menstruation, and menopause, which—alongside external stressors like work demands and family responsibilities—significantly affect mental health. To evaluate the mental health effects of these transitions, this study administered a Google Forms survey to 219 Indian women based on measures of symptom severity using a 1-5 rating scale. Participants were categorized into life stages: menarche (2.6%), active menstruation (74.3%), and menopause transition (23.1%). The analysis showed that factors like age, weight, and occupation notably influenced stress and mood, with heightened symptom severity observed among women in high-stress occupations during menstruation. Implications for practice and research are highlighted based on stressors and mental health needs across the different life stages.
